The level character is levChi V beta (flagL L), from levFn: the factor ext1 of the local level (P.H, P.chi) at rTup x is 1 for flagL and flag1L (subgroupCharExtension_one_apply), and the remaining factors are the products of L.cg (c+1) PP at dBlk (blkOf r t) (c+1) over c < s and of L.xq PP at dBlk (blk2 r) 1; levFn_flag1 makes the characters of flagL and flag1L agree. This is Tate's decomposition of the completed integers of K_infinity in the cyclotomic case, in an integral form with an explicit complement; the published Tate-Sen formalism [BC09, Section 14.1] states the rational decomposition with constants, so the book does not cite it for this form. GlobalTheory.Cyc.norm_primitiveRoot_sub_one (= T.norm_primitiveRoot_primePow_sub_one_padicComplex) and GlobalTheory.T.norm_mem_cyclotomic_layer_prime_rpow (= Cyc.norm_of_mem_Ks), for 1 <= j; the Lean writes the second as |x| = l^(n/(l^(j-1)(l-1))) for an integer n. The published result [Ser79, Chapter IV, Section 4] is that adjoining a primitive l^j-th root of unity zeta to an absolutely unramified complete field such as K_0 gives a totally ramified extension of degree l^(j-1)(l-1) with uniformizer zeta - 1; since |K_0^*| = l^Z and K_j = K_0(zeta), both statements follow. The Lean proves them its own way: the first from the value of the l^j-th cyclotomic polynomial at 1 (eval_one_cyclotomic_prime_pow) and the equality of the |1 - mu| over the primitive roots mu (norm_sub_one_le_of_isPrimitiveRoot); the second from the minimal polynomial of zeta over K_0, which is the l^j-th cyclotomic polynomial (minpoly_unramifiedSubfield_eq_cyclotomic), the values on K_0 (UnramValue.norm_of_mem_unramified_subfield) and the distinct absolute values of the terms of a polynomial in zeta - 1 of degree below l^(j-1)(l-1) (norm_aeval_of_norm_eq).

Part (1) is GlobalTheory.crysOnCond_all (CrysOnCond D HW F, through CrysOnLevel.isCrysOn_of_isCrys). GlobalTheory.T.ratio_invariant_in_K0 = Per.FracInv.tied_frac_invariant, with RegularRing.isDomain_of_tied, for the datum's period ring P.R.B under LocTied, read as Fontaine's B_cris. GlobalTheory.NL.N_basis_loc: a basis of (H.W K s LL h).N T over AA K LL = LetA (OL LL) n of size finrank_{OL LL} T, for IsCrys T. Its proof is WachFree.basis_of_regular with c = l: N_fg, N_base (IsBaseChange EE), EE_inj, injectivity of pi from EE_pi, and the l-saturation from W_proj through HWL.mem_smul_of_projective_comp (WachFree.mem_X_smul_of_projective); free_of_regular gives freeness over O[[X]] acting diagonally, and basis_of_baseChange (flatness over A and finrank_fibre at the maximal ideals of A) gives the A-basis. The book's last step uses the letters e_i N in place of the maximal ideals; the fibre rank is computed the same way. 259 lines.

GlobalTheory.T.wachLattice_heights_from_hodgeJumps = NL.Heights.heights_from_jumps, P5 D HW F, read for constant bounds M i = M0 and h i = h0 (jumpsLet_const, OverLetter): the first two clauses of p5 W T M h. The Lean's statement allows bounds that depend on the letter and has a third, saturation clause; neither is used. The proof follows heights_from_jumps at its top level, with the Lean's pole_bound as the second step and inv_pole_bound as the third, and its helper lemmas (mem_of_dvd, cancel_Q, conv_low, conv_lead, dvd_of_low, mem_of_low, low_of_mem, bdd_of_gens, indep_const, indep_lead) written into the steps. The inputs it cites are Lemmas -heights-points, -heights-division, -heights-letters, -heights-standard, -heights-full, -heights-basis and -heights-filtration, all written out, and no open step is left in their closure: Lemmas -full-image (the de Rham image of the Wach module) and -filtration-component (the Hodge filtration on a letter), the last two, are written out through Lemmas -full-image-sandwich, -filtration-component-split and -filtration-component-descent. The whole closure is 1,373 theorems, about 19,400 lines (theorems only) in 218 files by the count used here; an earlier count gave 960 theorems, about 14,300 lines in 188 files.

The level maps of the Wach data and the comparison data of the datum: LocWach.emb (emb_bij; the letters i of ZMod n are the embeddings K_0 -> L), DcrisL PD rho (emb i) (GlobalTheory.NL.Di), LocWach.lev (lev_letter, lev_pi: 1 + lev i zeta pi = C zeta * E with E(0) = 1 and E' = E, which is zeta exp(X) over a field of characteristic 0), and from the comparison CmpSit.tie : CmpTie, levB (= GlobalTheory.NL.ex) with levB_mem, levB_supp, levN_eq (W.levN = iotaV o levB), and levB_phi; levN_smul is the semilinearity of levN through lev. conv is GlobalTheory.NL.conv (a finsum, which is the finite sum here), Lambda is GlobalTheory.NL.Lat = latSpan (ex C h T i zeta), and F_tau^a is GlobalTheory.NL.FilAt PD T tau a. The book reads the datum's period rings as Fontaine's B_cris and B_dR, and iotaV as the inclusion. In (1), tau_(i+1) o sigma = tau_i is LocWach.emb_sigma, with sigma = PD.sigma and PD.phi_K0 (phi = sigma on K_0). (5) is CmpTie.levB_Gamma, with v the datum's valuation P.v LL (LocWach.v_l: v(l) = 1). (6) is CmpTie.betadR with betadR_tmul and levN_dR, for CmpSit.tie, whose iotadR is P.iotaB o AI.iotaA (A_inf into B_dR through B_cris), p1 = AI.pi_1 = [eps1] - 1, tS = l^(-s) iotaB(tB) and zS = zeta_{l^s}; levN_dR is stated with W.levN = iotaV o levB (levN_eq) and asks y with TWincl y = (1 tensor p1)^k jD(x). K_kappa is compKer T kappa and V tensor Fil^a is FilV a. (7) is two fields of the datum: LocAinf.ainf_image_mem_filtration_zero of D.locA (A_inf in Fil^0, through P.iotaB o AI.iotaA) and CmpSit.pi_1_inv of the comparison data (u in Fil^0 with p1 u = 1). The Lean takes both as hypotheses here; for Fontaine's B_dR they are theorems, with the locators given in (7): [BC09, (4.4.1), Corollary 4.4.5, Definition 4.4.7] for A_inf in B_dR^+ = Fil^0, [BC09, Proposition 4.4.6 and its proof] for B_dR^+ local with maximal ideal ker theta, and the formula for theta before [BC09, Lemma 4.4.1] for theta([eps^(1)]) = zeta_l. For its own construction of Fontaine's rings the Lean proves the first field (MemLoc.exists_locPrime_tied builds a LocAinf whose ainf_image_mem_filtration_zero is ExistsLocalPrimeAinf's fil0).

The fourth part of GlobalTheory.NL.lev_at_root_of_unity (for IsPrimitiveRoot zeta (l^s): lev i zeta Q = X * w with w a unit), through LevPt.lev_values; the proof follows lev_values (U = C zeta * E, X_eq, Q_eq, the product lev(Q) lev(X) = U^(l^s) - 1, coeff_one_pow_of_deriv and simple_zero). The Lean statement has six further parts, not used here.

The first part of GlobalTheory.NL.WDiv.weierstrass_dense: if a lies in van W i zeta k (X^k divides lev i zeta a) for every letter i and every primitive l^s-th root zeta in LL, then W.Q^k divides a in LetA O n. The statement has three further density parts, not used here. The proof follows Q_test: Q_eq and prod_prim (the cyclotomic polynomial as the product over the primitive roots in O, for mu0 from exists_prim), test = Per.weierstrass_test (X_pow_dvd_ev_iff, prime_X_sub_C, prod_prime_pow_dvd, with Mathlib's Weierstrass division in exists_div_X_sub_C), ev_X from lev_pi, lev_eq from lev_letter, and not_isUnit_sub_one. The facts about O[[X]] are cited from Lemmas is-onto-step-exp-bound-link-depth-norm-division (3) and is-onto-step-exp-bound-link-depth-norm-descent (4), which state the same mathematics and are proved in the Lean by other declarations (HeightDescentMinors.RootsProduct and HeightDescent).

The first part of GlobalTheory.NL.PhiD.phi_letters (Set.BijOn phiVB (Di (i-1)) (Di i)) and the first part of GlobalTheory.Per.LetterDim.tied_letter_component_finrank (finrank_LL (DcrisL PD rho tau) = finrank_LL V for IsCrys, given the count of embeddings, LevInj.card_emb), for the datum's tied period rings read in Fontaine's sense. phi_letters also states that the Di span D_cris, are independent, and that iotaV is injective; those parts are not used here. The proof follows PhiD.phi_bijOn (phi_mem, phi_injective, LocWach.emb_sigma) and Per.LetterDim.letter_eq: IsCrys (finrank D_cris = finrank K_0 * finrank V, which is Fontaine's crystallinity counted over L), DeRhamSplit.finrank_eq_sum (the decomposition by the idempotents of L tensor K_0, evalEmb_bijective), RegularRing.letter_le and RegularRing.exists_pow_sigma, which shows that sigma generates the embeddings from PD.fund (B_cris^(phi=1) meets Fil^0 in Q_l). The datum's period rings are read in Fontaine's sense: PD.phi_inj, PD.phi_comm and PD.phi_K0 (phi = sigma on K_0) are the facts cited from [BC09, 9.1], and PD.fund is the fundamental exact sequence. Most of the closure is the datum's period rings (isDomain_of_tied).

The third and last parts of GlobalTheory.NL.lev_at_root_of_unity: for zeta^(l^(s-1)) = 1, lev i zeta Q is a unit, and for every root of unity zeta of l-power order, lev i zeta Q is nonzero. The proof follows LevPt.lev_values (hQ, hXQ, hc1, hQone). The Lemma -standard-descent uses the nonvanishing where the Lean's full_down proves it as lev_Q_ne from CmpTie.lev_phi (the expansion of phi(f) is the rescaled expansion of f at (i-1, zeta^l)); both are Lean proofs of the same fact.

GlobalTheory.NL.GradedLat.zpow_ne_one applied to u = chi_Gamma(gam) with gam_gen, v_l, s_pos and s_two, together with ne_zero_of_val; the proof follows pow_ne_one (expand). AtZero.lower uses the same fact through chi_gam_zpow_ne_one, which the Lean proves from a norm estimate (LiftExp.norm_zpow_sub_one).

GlobalTheory.T.wachExpansionLattice_full_descends = NL.FullDown.full_down = full_down_generic: Full (Di i) (Lat i zeta) implies Full (Di (i-1)) (Lat (i-1) (zeta^l)) for a primitive l^j-th root zeta. Theta is the Lean's Tw (PD.p) phiVB. The proof follows full_down_generic: map_conv and Tw_conv, phi_inj, pow_mem (with N_phi, N_phiinv, N_fg), lev_Q_ne, conv_latSpan, phi_mem and full_of_conv.

GlobalTheory.T.wachExpansionLattice_graded_of_level_le = NL.GradedLat.graded_of_level_le = graded_Lat: Graded (Lat C h T i zeta) for zeta^(l^s) = 1, given Full. The proof follows graded_Lat: ex_gam (CmpTie.levB_Gamma for gam with a = 1), latSpan_stable, Per.single_mem_of_support_subset for (c), and graded_of_full.

GlobalTheory.NL.FullLevel.full_lat: Full (Di (HW l) h T i) (Lat C h T i zeta) for IsPrimitiveRoot zeta (l^s) and IsCrys T; Full asks for one m in N. The proof follows full_lat = FullLevel.full_of_span: Points.points (Lemma -full-embedding), EvdR.exists_ev_dR (Lemma -full-evaluation), the image Psi of wach_image_deRham_plus_component_level (Lemma -full-image), the dimension of Lemma -heights-letters, and the determinant argument of full_of_span (form, exists_det_ne_zero, exists_coord, eq_sum_ev) and full_of_det. The coordinates p_a of the proof are the Lean's form T iota (v.coord a), and K_kappa is compKer T iota.

GlobalTheory.NL.Points.points, first two parts: (1) is exists_pt (Pt (HW l) h i zeta tau: some tau_s on K_s with IsPt, i.e. tau_s = emb i on K_0 and tau_s(zetaQ s) = zeta, restricting to tau), and (2) is pt_props, whose map iota (the book's kappa) is Comp: iota(emb i c) = c on K_0, iota(zeta) = zetaQ s and iota(tau c) = c on K. The irreducibility of the cyclotomic polynomial over K_0 is Cyc.minpoly_unramifiedSubfield_eq_cyclotomic, cited from [Ser79, IV.4]. The Lean's further parts (every tau lies over some (i, zeta), and the counts of embeddings) are not used here; the count for K_0 is part of Definition -expansions (1).

GlobalTheory.NL.EvdR.exists_ev_dR = exists_ev_tied = Bridge.exists_power_series_evaluation, for the datum's B_dR read in Fontaine's sense: tS P s = l^(-s) iotaB(tB), with tB the datum's t. The Lean proves the properties of B_dR^+ it needs from the datum's axioms (mem_zero_of_isIntegral, tS_mem_iff, reduction); the book cites them from [BC09, Proposition 4.4.6 (B_dR^+ a complete discrete valuation ring), Definition 4.4.7 (B_dR its fraction field, Fil^a the powers of the maximal ideal) and Proposition 4.4.8 (t a uniformizer)]. The evaluation is the limit of the truncations (exists_ev, exists_lim), and the divisibility criterion is ev_dvd_iff.

GlobalTheory.T.frobenius_integrality_tensor_ainf_coefficients = FrobIntegralCoeff.frobenius_integrality_coeff, for RW LL = O_L tensor W(C_l^flat) with phiRW and RA LL = O_L tensor A_inf (inclR). The reduction to O = Z_l is integrality_baseChange (regRep, blow, eq_sum_regRep, mem_range_of_regRep), as in the book; the case O = Z_l is T.frobeniusIntegrality_wittTilt_ainf (FrobInt.frobenius_integrality: valuationRing_tilt and perfectRing_Cb, then integral_of_frobenius), which the book follows through Lemmas -decompletion-frobenius-tilt and -decompletion-frobenius-witt. Here C_l^flat is the Lean's Cb l, the fraction field of the tilt OCb l = PreTilt (OC l) l, and A_inf = W(OCb l) sits in W(Cb l) through inclW.

GlobalTheory.FrobInt.valuationRing_tilt (through dvd_total_tilt) and FrobInt.perfectRing_Cb, for OCb l = PreTilt (OC l) l, Mathlib's perfection of O_C/l, and Cb l = FractionRing (OCb l); the bijectivity of Frobenius on OCb l is Mathlib's frobeniusEquiv for the perfection. These are [BC09, section 4.3, Lemma 4.3.3 (R is the valuation ring of v_R) and Theorem 4.3.5 (Frac R is algebraically closed, hence perfect)]; the Lean's proof of the valuation-ring property, through the sharp roots and divisibility in O_C, is BC09's. About 110 lines.

GlobalTheory.FrobInt.residue_integral, for a valuation ring R with fraction field K (IsFractionRing) and matrices indexed by finite types; the Lean uses ValuationRing.valuation R K and chooses the entry of largest value by Finset.exists_max_image. The exponent is the prime l.

GlobalTheory.FrobInt.integral_of_frobenius, for a valuation ring R of characteristic l with PerfectRing R l, its fraction field K with PerfectRing K l and CharP K l, the Frobenius WittVector.map (frobenius K l) and the inclusion WittVector.map (algebraMap R K). Its proof is FrobInt.step (the first step), approx (the second) and the comparison of coefficients through WittVector.truncate (the last). The Witt-vector facts are Mathlib's (WittVector.mem_span_p_pow_iff_le_coeff_eq_zero, p_nonzero, teichmuller, constantCoeff); the book cites Serre's Local Fields for them.

GlobalTheory.NL.SandArb.sandwich: for IsCrys T there is m with, for x in N T, inclR(E.io W.X)^m jD(x) in the range of TWincl (R_A tensor T in R tensor T), and (inclR(E.io W.X)^m) tensor t in the O-span of the inclR(a) jD(y). The formula for varpi is IoXQ.io_X (io_X_gen, teich_pow: E.io W.X = 1 tensor pi_1 with AI.pi_1 = [eps1] - 1). SandArb.sandwich applies sand_layers through apply_layers, that is HWL.SandProof.sandwich for the layers built from the datum, and of_layers to return to the datum's Wach module (nOf_crys); building the layers needs AllLaws.laws (wachLevelExpansionLaws_of_rootsOfUnity, wach_etale_map_frobenius_galois_equivariant, isCrys_lat_of_trivial), which the argument of sand_of does not use. HWL.SandProof.sandwich takes the basis from wach_lattice_free_of_crystalline (HWL.lattice_free, which is WachFree.basis_of_regular as in Lemma -inputs-basis), phi_R(x) = x io(Q) from frobenius_inclusion_X_eq_mul_Q with Sandwich.phiRW_teichmuller and x_eq, and runs sand_of: hsp and hli (the R-basis, as in part (2) of Lemma -inputs), uniform (the exponent m), and Sandwich.upper and Sandwich.lower with frobenius_integrality_coeff (Lemma -decompletion-frobenius) for the two inclusions. This is the argument of Lemma -decompletion-sandwich, run with the exponent from the Wach module's own bounds in place of M0 and h0. The closure of SandArb.sandwich is 310 theorems, about 3,900 lines by the count used here: AllLaws.laws about 1,900 and wachInclusion_X_Q_frobenius about 1,700 (of which io_X is about 80 and the injectivity of inclR, TensorWitt.main, about 500); sand_of with upper and lower is about 250.

GlobalTheory.T.wach_image_deRham_plus_component_level = NL.PerS.image, for (i, zeta, tau, iota) with Comp: Psi x lies in FilV 0 (V tensor Fil^0), (1) is hspan (z - sum b_j Psi(x_j) in compKer T iota with b_j in Fil 0), and (2) is the third clause, with compKer T iota = K_kappa and FilV the image of V tensor Fil. The Lean statement does not ask zeta to be a primitive l^s-th root of unity; the book states it for those zeta, the case Lemma -heights-full uses. The proof follows PerS.image = PerS.core = core_gen: m and Y from SandArb.sandwich (Lemma -full-image-sandwich), hX = io_X and hinj (inclR injective, HWL.TensorWitt.main; the book takes R_A as a subring of R, Definition -data, and the injectivity on R_A tensor T is TWincl_injective), hi = EmbFil.emb_mem_fil_zero (fact (b), Lemma -full-evaluation(1)), and u from CmpSit.pi_1_inv with A_inf in Fil^0 from AI.ainf_image_mem_filtration_zero (fact (a)). These two are fields of the datum, stated in the book as Definition -expansions(7); for Fontaine's B_dR they hold by [BC09, (4.4.1), Corollary 4.4.5, Proposition 4.4.6, Definition 4.4.7] and the formula for theta before [BC09, Lemma 4.4.1], as (7) says. In core_gen: Psi x = u^m betadR(Y x), betadR_mem_FilV and mulVR_FilV; (2) is Ct.levN_dR (Definition -expansions (6)) with mulVR_sup; (1) is gen_form, mulVR_gen and mem_gen for G = Gen, act_betadR (fact (d)), hA' and hB (the span S), ht1 with TWincl_injective, and hv. core_gen with its helpers is about 420 lines; the closure of PerS.image is 547 theorems, about 6,800 lines by the count used here (an earlier count gave 589 theorems, about 7,600 lines), almost all in the sandwich, IoXQ.main and emb_mem_fil_zero.

The second part of GlobalTheory.NL.LevInj.expansion_basis, for every basis nb : Basis (Fin r) (LetA O n) (N T): (1) the uniqueness of the coefficients, (2) the span, (3) the shift criterion with van W i zeta k. Its first part, the semilinearity of the expansions, is fact (a) of the proof of Lemma -inputs-heights (LevInj.lift_smul). The hypotheses are IsCrys T, a primitive l^j-th root zeta for some j, and Full for (i, zeta). The proof follows LevInj.core' and LevInj.core: the module S of sequences bounded below is the Lean's Hahn module (coeff_smul_hahn), and the linear independence is indep_of_span through linearIndependent_iff_card_le_finrank_span; the bound r <= dim D_i(V) is card_eq_rank (DD_free, N_base), rank_le and Lemma -heights-letters.

GlobalTheory.T.wach_lattice_eq_std_powerSeries_at_zero = NL.AtZero.lat_one_std: Std (Di i) (Lat i 1). The proof follows lat_one_std: down (full_descends applied s times, starting from full_lat at a primitive l^s-th root; the Lean takes the root from exists_isPt_primitiveRoot), graded_of_level_le at zeta = 1, uniform_supp, AtZero.lower (third step: N_Gamma, N_pi, CmpTie.levB_Gamma with zeta = zeta' = 1 and j = a = 0, Model.pi_van_one, chi_gam_zpow_ne_one) and std_of_lower (fourth to last steps).

GlobalTheory.NL.LatLow.lat_low: Std (Di (HW l) h T i) (Lat C h T i zeta) for zeta^(l^(s-1)) = 1 and IsCrys T. The proof follows lat_low: induction on j with zeta^(l^j) = 1, the base case zeta = 1 being wach_lattice_eq_std_powerSeries_at_zero = AtZero.lat_one_std (Lemma -standard-one) and the step LatLow.std_step with the third part of wachLevel_expansion_at_root_of_unity (Lemma -standard-values), Lemma -heights-letters, N_phi, N_phiinv and CmpTie.levB_phi. No open step is left in its closure; the base case uses Lemma -heights-full, which rests on Lemma -full-image.

The first part of GlobalTheory.NL.Points.points (for IsPrimitiveRoot zeta (l^s) there is tau with Pt (HW l) h i zeta tau: some tau_s on K_s with IsPt, restricting to emb i on K_0 and sending the datum's zeta_{l^s} to zeta, and extending tau) combined with GlobalTheory.NL.LatFil.lat_eq_fil for that tau: f in Lat iff f is bounded below, f k in Di and iotaV (f k) in FilAt tau (-k) for every k. The book states the existence of tau without the property Pt, which the proof of Lemma -inputs-heights does not use; the proof chooses tau as in Lemma -full-embedding, which is Pt. The proof follows lat_eq_fil at its top level: graded_of_level_le (Lemma -standard-graded) with full_lat, and the main step from deRhamComponent_wachLetter_basis_filtration (Lemma -filtration-component) and single_mem_iff (Lemma -filtration-single), with mem_sup_iff for the coordinates. No open step is left in its closure.

The second part of GlobalTheory.T.deRhamComponent_wachLetter_basis_filtration: for d in Di, iotaV d in FilAt PD T tau a iff iotaV d in compKer T iota + FilV a, for (i, zeta, tau, iota) with Comp and tau = emb i on K_0. Its other parts (independence over B_dR of an L-independent family of Di in V tensor_iota B_dR, the projection of the tau-part of D_dR onto Di, and finrank Di = finrank V) are not used by lat_eq_fil. The proof follows CompD.filAt_iff, the part of component_tied that gives this clause: iota_mem (PD.iota_comm), others_le_compKer, exists_part (the idempotent splitting exists_sum = exists_proj on DdR, with DeRhamSplit.mul_mem_DdR), and hkey = mem_FilV_local (Lemma -filtration-component-descent); the count of embeddings K -> L is hc from Points.points (card_emb, through exists_aut and exists_restr from Good K s LL). It uses only d in D_cris (not d in Di) and the third clause of Comp (iota o tau = id on K). The closure of component, 846 theorems and about 11,000 lines, is almost all in the unused parts (ddR_le through isDR_of_isCrys, tied_deRham_span, tied_letter_component_finrank); filAt_iff with mem_FilV_local is about 400 lines, besides the field property of B_dR (isField_of_tied), which the book cites.

GlobalTheory.NL.CompD.exists_proj, for fields F, K (the book's E) and L (the book's L') with Fintype.card (K ->a[F] L) = finrank F K, commuting F-algebra maps alpha : L -> End_F M and beta : K -> End_F M: e sigma = Psi (Phi^-1 (Pi.single sigma 1)) with Psi = Algebra.TensorProduct.lift alpha beta and Phi the algebra equivalence of GlobalTheory.DeRhamSplit.evalEmb_bijective (L tensor_F K ~ functions on the embeddings). evalEmb_bijective proves surjectivity from linearIndependent_monoidHom (Dedekind-Artin independence of characters, [Lan02, VI, Theorem 4.1]) and injectivity by comparing dimensions. The Lean states (4) for additive subgroups N stable under alpha and beta, as here.

GlobalTheory.NL.CompD.mem_FilV_local, for T : Lt K LL, tau, iota with iota (tau c) = c on K, a in Z and y in DdRE (P.PD K) T.rho tau (the tau-part D_tau): y in compKer T iota + FilV a implies y in FilV a. The proof follows mem_FilV_local and mem_FilV_of_comp with E = Om l: exists_factor (the first step; it needs IsDomain BdR, from RegularRing.isField_of_tied), exists_proj (Lemma -filtration-component-split) for L tensor Q_l-bar acting on V tensor BdR, exists_conj with Points.exists_aut (g = g1 g0^-1), act_compKer, act_FilV, om_mul_mem_Fil and mu_FilV (third step, hk), and h6, h7 (fourth step). The datum's BdR is read as Fontaine's: the field property, Q_l-bar in Fil^0 with Fil^0 Fil^a in Fil^a (the Lean's om_mul_mem_Fil, through P.PD_Fil), and the G_K-action preserving Fil^a and restricting to the Galois action on Q_l-bar (P.PD_actdR, P.actQdR_Om, PD.Fil_G) are cited from [BC09]: the field property and the filtration from Proposition 4.4.6 and Definition 4.4.7 (B_dR = Frac(B_dR^+), Fil^a the a-th power of the maximal ideal, G_K-stable), and Q_l-bar inside B_dR^+ with its Galois action from Lemma 4.4.10. In the Lean all of these except the field property are fields of the datum (LocPrime and PeriodData: actQdR_Om, PD_actdR, Fil_G, Fil_mul, and Fil^a a K-submodule with PD_Fil). The field property is not a field of the datum: the Lean proves it (isField_of_tied: bdR_isField for its own Per.BdR, carried to the datum's ring by the ring isomorphism eD of the tie D.locT; 224 theorems, about 2,500 lines).

GlobalTheory.NL.LatFil.single_mem_iff as lat_eq_fil applies it (main), with mem_sup_iff to read compKer + FilV a through the coordinates crd T iota (bV.coord alpha). The Lean's single_mem_iff is an abstract statement about a filtered ring R, t, ev, coordinates p and Psi; the book states it for the datum. 'Expands at shift a' is the Lean's Rep; the steps are key (a), hA (b), hspan' (c), hli (d) and hB (e).

GlobalTheory.NLink.wAll_holds (WAll D HW F) = T.wachHypothesis_crystallineLattices = WachHyp.hypW_crystalline, from UsedLocalConclusion, ConclusionE and CrysOnCond (Lemma asm-two-three-killing-wach-frame-exists-inputs), stated for one (K, s, LL) with Good K s LL. The proof follows WachHyp.wClauses and HypW_of_rec: nBasis for (a); for (b) and (c) the Lean writes N as the supremum of its letter parts Nl Y i = e_i N, which it takes from WachLatticeFree (wachFree, first part; part (4) of Lemma asm-two-three-killing-wach-frame-exists-inputs), and inducts over the supremum with P5W through jumpsLet_const and jump_mem, as the book does; (d) is N_Gamma and N_pi, (e) is map_N. Size of wAll_holds: 2,655 theorems, about 41,100 lines in 557 files, of which wClauses is 4 theorems and 90 lines.

asm-theta-agree-real-quotient-fock-facts: The statements are hypotheses in Formalism.PeriodIntegrals.OrbitalBoundsConclusion, proved in Formalism.PeriodIntegrals.UnitaryGroupMassFormula: (1) is FockH1Action.H1 (gradedOscillatorProperty), whose adjointness clauses the book does not use; (2) is HarmSplit (harmonicSplitting_holds) for (u1, u2) = (true, false) and (true, true); (3) is JointMult (fock_joint_multiplicity, from cauchy_highest_weight) with ShapeOf (shapeOf_of_cauchy); (4) is the first half of OneDeg (fock_degree_one), whose hypothesis OfType is the finite-dimensional subspace of the statement; (5) is the first half of WtDeg (highestWeightDegree_le); (6) is Swap.hwHarmDeg2 with hwHarmDeg_of; (7) is the first half of MinDegJ (minimal_degree_joint); (8) is hwExist2, from PI.FockOneDegW.hwExist. Relation to the literature: (2) is Howe's decomposition of the Fock space into harmonics and the image of the raising operators [How89]; (3), (4) and (7) are the correspondence of K-types on joint harmonics and its degree property, which [How89] gives for a reductive dual pair and [KV78] makes explicit for the pairs (U(k), U(p,q)); the description by joint shapes for (U(P,Q), U(R,S)) is the Lean's own form of that correspondence; (1), (5) and (8) are standard. The Lean proves all of them in its own way.
asm-theta-agree-real-quotient-fock-rules: (1) adj1 and adj2 (fock_inner_adjoint_first and _second, from rai_adj, low_adj, omE_adj_gen), with fock_kernel_adjoint for the same block; (2) Harm.mp_comm with homogComponent_comm_first_action and _second_action; (3) harmonic_stable_*, jHarmonic_stable_*, homogeneous_stable_* and polChi_stable_second_action, and PI.FJMF.jset_hc; (4) Delta_{bb'} is PI.FockOneDegW.lowOp b b' (Harm.minusPart_second_action_Eab), with low_homog, low_homog_small, second_action_add_lowering, harmonic_stable_lowering, polChi_low, low_comm and mem_jHarm_iff; (5) scalar_of_hw (through low_kill and norm_low) and mem_polChi_iff_hw; (6) dom2 (dom_of_hw) and supp2 (supp_col_pos and supp_col_neg, a computation with the monomials of g).
asm-theta-agree-real-quotient-split: (1) charSplit (CoreSplit.lean), with K the span of the images of the D a b and y from PI.FHS.exists_orth; (2) polChi_small (with highestWeightDegree_le) and th_small; (3) th_plus1; (4) th_next, with harmonicSplitting_holds for (true, false). asm-theta-agree-real-quotient-lie-module: A Lie module is act : Mat R S ->l End T with IsLie; the stable subspace generated by a set is genG; the compact Casimir operator is casK (units act), and c(mu) is casW mu, where posC a b means a < b in the same block. asm-theta-agree-real-quotient-filtration: cas_bound_gl, the case of the abstract cas_bound with e_k = act(E_ab) for the pairs in the same block (KI), X_i = act(E_ab) for the pairs in different blocks (PIx), c_k = adC k and d = R + S. Facts (a) and (b) are h1' and h2' (pc_ad, kc_mul, pc_sum, kc_sum); (c) is adC_sw and (d) is adC_cas (adad_apply, count_cross). asm-theta-agree-real-quotient-local: local_of. asm-theta-agree-real-one-place: onePlace, reduced to onePlaceD by checking RealData.Hyp with omega; the Lean's (a - a')/2 is natural-number division of a truncated difference, which agrees with the floor because the inequality forces a > a'. asm-theta-agree-real-parity: Parity, proved by even_im_hermitian_sub: resalpha and resbeta (ResEtaPow) and expalpha and expbeta (HasExp) evaluated at sgnId w, with hasExp_sgn.
asm-theta-agree-real-frames: FrameEx, with HasSig and IsCartan of WeilTensorModels; the signature in the statement is HasSig. frameEx applies frame_conj to the entrywise conjugates of M, theta and B; frame_conj uses diag_ex (a factorization N = P*P from CStarAlgebra.isStrictlyPositive_iff_eq_star_mul_self and the eigenvector unitary of a Hermitian matrix) and inertia_le, which is Sylvester's law of inertia.
asm-theta-agree-real-lines: GenEx, LineEx and KLine. genEx uses exists_gen_matrix, which the Lean proves by differentiating A(t) times the integral of A over [0, epsilon] (hasDerivAt_oneParam, eq_exp_of_hasDerivAt); the text cites [Hal15, Theorem 2.14] for this fact. asm-theta-agree-real-weak: ActsLaws, proved by actsLaws: clause (1) is SD to ActsD, (2) is SA to Acts, and (3) collects the uniqueness for ActsD, Acts and SD. Facts (a) to (d) are exists_SB, eval_adm, exists_of_rest (with slice_mem) and eq_of_pureA.
asm-theta-agree-real-derivative: DerEx, for an arbitrary Darboux structure d on symp, of which only the A-linearity of d.e is used; the operator is dopL of the components at infinity (IsD). asm-theta-agree-real-tensor: tensor_irr: tensor_nontrivial, upq_decomp, stable_all with GlobalTheory.IrrTensor.density (a form of the Jacobson density theorem that the Lean proves), stable_map, exists_prodForm_ne and irr_of_stable.
asm-theta-agree-real-fock-map: (1) is FockEx, for any Darboux structure d, which is the isomorphism e of the text, with Framed (a b = I); a Fock map for a model is one for its isomorphism (M.co). IsFockMap is the Fock map property. Coordinates: exists_lift (untw, tw, tw1); the form: hform with herm_frame, trace_J and trace_trace; the Heisenberg structure Heis (v, lam, D, form, dim) of exists_heis. The vacuum: exists_sec, vac_iff, exists_vac (exists_schwartz_cexp). The Fock map: exists_fockMap with exists_fock, hop, and iota, iota_hop, heisOp_eq, iota_sumPl. asm-theta-agree-real-metaplectic: (1) is quad_eq, with quad the Lean's definition (4 pi i)^-1 sum over a, b of ((X J)_ab / 2)(dRho e_a dRho e_b + dRho e_b dRho e_a), J = Matrix.J, sympl = -w^T J w'; rho_S is rhoS (phase, rhoFun) and d rho is dRho. (2) is LocalLift, with implementation meaning Impl (norm and impl), equivalently Im. It is a form of the existence of the metaplectic representation [Wei64], [Fol89, Chapter 4]; the Lean proves it as localLift_holds, with V(t) = big (inverse of the block A(t) of exp(tX), B(t), C(t), |det A(t)|^(-1/2)), a composite of a quadratic phase, a dilation and Fourier transforms (IsoOfIntegral, NormExpSubLe, HasDerivAtSchwartzToL2); the constant of (2) is the derivative at 0 of |det A(t)|^(-1/2) plus half the trace of the upper left block of X. GlobalTheory.Published.RealMetaplecticRepresentation, a global form of the same published result, is not used on this route. (3) is Im.covD and Im.quad.
asm-theta-agree-real-projective: mid2, for W the infinite places and SG K, LG K the group and Lie algebra; HS K rho is H (SG K intersected with HG rho), and A is the homomorphism of the hypothesis. (i) is exists_im; (ii) is line with exists_avg, bd_of_conf and bdd_of_weak (Banach-Steinhaus); (iii) is the additivity in scalar_lie through delta_zero (tele_lim, norm_le_lin), strong (taylor2), dif_mul and pow_lim, with exp_mul_inj; (iv) is hAd' with Im.quad; (v) is real_form_trace and eq_trace, with lie_of_exp.
asm-theta-agree-real-oscillator: main2. Its hypotheses are IsUSplitting for om (pres, impl with actB, adm, unit, cont), the matrices K with hK, hu and hKJ, and IsD for the operators D of Lemma asm-theta-agree-real-derivative; the pairs (u_j, v_j) are indexed by an arbitrary finite type. The coordinates are Co (exists_co, with P, P', vec, schr_P, P_dRho, sympl_vec, sympl_e); iota is exists_iota (exists_lf, ext_at, map_form); rho_R is built from Ee and Rm (hrho, hact, hsp with hTens_actB and mem_sp_of). The Schur step is step with Co.schur2: the finite places use eq_zero_of_mul_invariant, and the archimedean place uses Delta.eq_delta', which the Lean proves with Hadamard's lemma and density of compactly supported functions (RLLieD) where the text cites [Hor90, Theorem 2.3.4]. A is built from A0 with uniq; continuity is exists_adm with hom.cont; then mid2, quad_eq and IsD.P.
asm-theta-agree-real-lie: (1) is LieSecond and (2) is LieFirst, stated in the Lean's form: for any Darboux structure d, which is the isomorphism e of the text, for a representation om of U_W, respectively of U_X, that satisfies only IsUWeilB (condition (a) of a Weil representation for (1), and condition (b), through the transposed Darboux structure d' with d'.e(x^T) = d.e(x), for (2)), and for a character chi in Chr F E, a homomorphism from the ideles of E to the circle, with HasExp. The conclusion is ActsBy with c = m/2. The proofs are lieSecond2 (main2 twice, fock_data, and the comparisons step2 and step1) and lieFirst (sw, sw_heis, sw_fock), which applies LieSecond to (JB, JA, d', b, a, C, A) and the Fock map composed with the swap.
asm-theta-agree-finite: KFin, discharged by kFin_of FinRam FinSplit FinInert, which assembles FinMaps from local data IsFinAt: FinRam for v in X.T, FinInert if there is no F-embedding E -> F_v, FinSplit otherwise.
asm-theta-agree-finite-unique: KCo.ActsUniq, proved as KCo.action_uniqueness with the test function r equal to a bump function at infinity (exists_sinf) times the indicator functions of the integral vectors at the finite places other than v.
asm-theta-agree-finite-split-models: omega_A and omega_B are SplitFlip.omA and omB, with |x|^z = apow x z (nabs, the normalized absolute value). Unitary is norm 1, smooth is CondLE (trivial on unitCong (varpi^e)), unramified is SplitWeil.IsUnram. I(alpha,beta) is SplitLoc.indSp, with the factor indFac and IsBlockUpper; R is rtr. 'Reads as' is KCo.Reads.
asm-theta-agree-finite-bernstein: The Lean's input is NarrowBernstein (BernsteinRamification.NarrowBern): for unitary smooth chi_1, chi_2 with a != b or chi_1 != chi_2, prod2 (detRep a chi_1) (detRep b chi_2) is irreducible. indIrredLt_of and indIrredNarrow_of transfer it to submodules of indSp through toFn and exists_toFn, in the form IndIrredLt (a' < a) used here. narrowBern derives it from Published.GeometricLemmaFiltration, the filtration of the geometric lemma of Bernstein and Zelevinsky [BZ77, 2.12], through SmGL.Bernstein.prod2_detRep_isIrreducible; so the Lean proves this case its own way. I(alpha,beta) is the normalized parabolic induction of (alpha o det) x (beta o det) from the block upper triangular parabolic, whose modulus character is |det b_A|^{a'} |det b_D|^{-a}. Bernstein [Ber84] proves that a product of irreducible unitary representations of general linear groups is irreducible, which contains this statement without the condition a != a' or alpha != beta.
asm-theta-agree-finite-iwasawa: SplitDict.IndIwasawa, proved as induced_vanish_of_vanish_on_integral from iwasawa_blockTriangular and law_parab.
asm-theta-agree-finite-zeta: Part (1) is RamMaps and RamNonzero (ramMaps_of, and ramified_map_ne_zero = pRam_ne_zero) for pRam = bigP and pRam' = smallP, which are Z and Z' of Lemma th-bottom-split-zeta for the Haar measures haarVol (KO k (Fin a)) and haarVol (KO k (Fin a')). Part (2) is UnrMaps (unrMaps_of_lt) for pUnr and pUnr': zetaUnr is zeta, zCoeff is z_m, invL is P_r, and pUnr' = (invL a' d).eval 1 times smallP. Both are stated under HidaSetting, which records a' < a, d even, unitary alpha and beta, nu = alpha/beta and the smoothness of alpha and beta; IsUnram nu follows from IsUnram alpha and IsUnram beta (isUnram_nu). RamMaps and UnrMaps also contain the surjectivity onto indSp, which the Lean derives from irreducibility (onto_of_irred, onto_of_irredLt); here it is derived in the proofs of Lemmas asm-theta-agree-finite-ramified and -split. The proof is given as a computation with its result; the Lean's shells are the cells K varpi^n K (cell, shellSet).
asm-theta-agree-finite-characters: SplitAsm.ChrFacts, proved as split_character_facts from Chars.IsGood (heckeAlpha, heckeBeta, ram, unrAlpha, unrBeta) and GaussNonvanish.exists_condLE. The characters are chrW X.alpha tau and so on.
asm-theta-agree-finite-local-objects: L_v is latW and K_Y(v) is KAt (the subgroup KSub); a Lagrangian is IsLagAt, adapted is IsAdaptedAt, P_C is PAt and P_C^x is Sph.PSub; an evaluation form is IsEvAt; local operators are IsLocRep (fields pres, acts, one, mul, smooth, presH, actsH, impl). In IsLocRep the action at v is an equivalence: om(g,h) acts at v by phi -> phi_1 if and only if phi_1 = omega_v(g,h) phi; with Lemma asm-theta-agree-finite-unique this is the condition stated here. The Lean's omega_v is defined on all of UA x UA, with conditions only for g and h at v.
asm-theta-agree-finite-inputs: (1) is SplitDict.Dict (DictAt for every F-embedding tau), proved as split_place_dictionary; gamma, gamma' and eta are inB tau b, inB tau b' and inB tau c. (2) is LocRepEx (locRepEx) with IsLocRep.smoothX. (3) is stabiliser_compact, isCompact_KAt (for V and V') and FinSt (finSt); (4) is CartanSt (cartanSt2); (5) is ThKH.Iwas.iwasawa, whose further clause, on characters of K_W(v) trivial on P_C and K_W(v), is not used; (6) is EvVac (ThKH.Evl.evVac), EvInvSt (evInvSt) and SiegSt (siegSt), stated in the Lean for every pair satisfying PairOK at an inert place, here for the two pairs of the triple, with |.| the modulus (sbClass (Fv F v)).modu; (7) is ModSt (modSt2), with Mathlib's relIndex, which is 0 for an infinite index. The Lean states (3), (4) and (7) for a skew-Hermitian W of a good base at an inert place. The proofs of (2), (3), (4), (5) and (7) follow the Lean: (2) is locRepEx, with the local operators res x_0 (omega(g,h)(phi tensor r_0)) and res x_0 (rho(u)(phi tensor r_0)), the Lean's loc (om p) and loc (schrL psi (M.co.e u)); the commutation of omega(g,h) with rho(u) for u with zero v-components is act_away and IsUWeilPair.isUSplitting; the action of rho(u) for u at v is SchrLoc.schr_tens_of_at; the smoothness in U_X is IsLocRep.smoothX. (3) is isCompact_KAt (kc_bound, kc_mat, isCompact_of_units) and finSt (finSt_KGL through the frame); (4) and (5) transport Theorem asm-theta-agree-finite-inputs-bruhat-tits through the frame, as cartanSt2 and iwasawa do; (7) transports Lemma asm-theta-agree-finite-inputs-modulus, as modSt_of does with chart and locMod. The proof of (1) follows split_place_dictionary: the split bases are the bases b_v at v in B.P with tau = tau_v and delta = 1 (the fields bas and psiP), and otherwise come from exists_isSplitBasis and exists_cond; model_alt and model_Bar (Lemma asm-theta-agree-dictionary-models) give iota and iota', with chrW_conj and chrW_div for the characters, and dictX gives the surjectivity of inB tau c. The proof of (6) follows evVac, evInvSt and siegSt. evVac takes the form from LagFun.exists_invariant_form (Lemma asm-theta-agree-finite-inputs-invariant) and its value at the vacuum from core (Lemma asm-theta-agree-finite-inputs-criterion), with space_split, lat_split and mem_latAtV_of_dual; the last proves Lemma asm-theta-agree-evaluation-lattice(2) again, for psi_v of conductor O_v (PsiUnr), and the book cites that lemma. evInvSt and siegSt pass to the local pair of ThKH.Locpair.locPairEx (Lemma asm-theta-agree-finite-inputs-local-pair) with PT.isHerm_loc, PT.isSkew_loc, PT.isLagr_loc, PT.isEv_of, PT.actsX and PT.actsW, and apply split_character_fixes_evaluation (Lemma asm-theta-agree-finite-inputs-fixed) with EvInv.locChar_one, respectively siegel_transport (Lemma asm-theta-agree-finite-inputs-transport) with L.chX. The adaptedness of C is a hypothesis of EvInvSt and SiegSt that their proofs do not use.
asm-theta-agree-finite-inputs-invariant: GlobalTheory.CompanionTheory.LagFun.exists_invariant_form, for a k-subspace large_2 with w.1 . w'.2 = w'.1 . w.2 for all its elements; exists_param gives j, sigma and the left inverse p. The Lean extends the integral from the subspace of the phi with t -> g(t) phi(j t) integrable by LinearMap.exists_extend, and takes U clopen, containing 0, inside a compact set on which Re g(p x) > 0. The hypothesis that psi is not 1 is not used.
asm-theta-agree-finite-inputs-criterion: ThKH.Evl.core, stated with the hypotheses that psi is continuous, of absolute value 1 and not 1; a continuous character of k has absolute value 1. The reduction to the translates of phi_0 is cyc, which takes the cyclicity of the Schrödinger representation from VacLoc.ModelLine.cyclic_and_line, through SchrSys.exists_isModel and GoodInh.exists_goodChar; this is Theorem asm-theta-agree-dictionary-stone-von-neumann(1).
asm-theta-agree-finite-inputs-uniqueness: (1) is ThKH.Evl.mem_of_orth, (2) is exists_test and (3) is line, for a subspace of finrank |kappa|. In (2) the vanishing on functions that vanish on j(k^r) is the step van, through GlobalTheory.WeilM.eq_zero_of_mul_invariant, which argues by induction over compact sets; the fourth step is transl, which applies core to the translations.
asm-theta-agree-finite-inputs-averaging: ThK.LinAct.exists_avg, with exists_section for S, coeff_mem for F_phi (through eventually_fix and exists_compact_ann, which bounds the annihilator with a good character) and cyc for (1). |det g| is distribHaarChar k (det g), and the change of variables is integral_comp_mulVec.
asm-theta-agree-finite-inputs-local-data: The local data are the Lean's objects for the test class sbClass k, in which every linear form is admissible and the modulus is distribHaarChar k, the normalized absolute value. The form is symp c (-1) J_A J_B, the trace of -hTens; a local Darboux isomorphism is Darboux, a local splitting is IsSplitting for actB c (whose field adm is empty here), the local Siegel rule is SiegelRule, a local Weil datum is IsWeilB (with IsDblCoord, dbl and diagCols) and a local Weil pair is IsWeilPair. asm-theta-agree-dictionary-action: KCo.acts_formula, for IsWeilB (obtained from the halves of IsWeil by IsUWeilB.isWeilB, which forgets unitarity and continuity); its scalar is chrW chi t (gdet g_0) times apow (gdet g_0) (card alpha / 2), with card alpha = n. asm-theta-agree-coinvariants-split: GoodSplit, for a good base (whose fields include that E is CM and Galois over Q), proved by good_split_of_cm through Ideal.sum_ramification_inertia_eq_finrank, Ideal.ncard_primesOver_mul_ramificationIdxIn_mul_inertiaDegIn and AdelicU.nonempty_split_iff.
asm-theta-agree-coinvariants-nontrivial: NuSt, proved by nu_statement: chrW X.nu t ≠ 1. The first paragraph is hall; the generator pi_0 comes from the finiteness of the class group (pow_card_eq_one'); the roots of unity are exists_pow_eq_one, through exists_level; the archimedean identity is arch_eq_one with hasExp_div hC.expα hC.expβ and fin_eq_one (FrobDense.eq_one_of_local); m > 0 is hT.geo.kappa; the last paragraph is not_prod, with eq_one_of_smul for the trivial decomposition group and exists_cm_conj_ne.
asm-theta-agree-coinvariants-kernel: Part (1) is KCo.exists_full and part (2) is KCoNarrow.ker_eq_ne, the variant of KCo.ker_eq for IrrStNe. Both are stated in the Lean, and here, for any representation om of U_X x U_W on the functions on A_F^I, for lattice spaces X and W, and any linear map iota that is bijective on Schwartz-Bruhat functions and satisfies IsDict. exists_full needs neither n ≤ d nor USm alpha, which only ker_eq_ne uses. Lemma asm-theta-agree-coinvariants applies the lemma to the representations omega and omega' of a triple.
asm-theta-agree-convergence: ThK.WeilConv. The bound is on the Bochner integral of the norm of the theta function, and the continuity is that of f -> I(pureA f phi)(h) on SchwartzMap. The proof is ThKEst.weilConv hSiegelSet thetaBasic = weilConv_of thetaBasic (domWeil_of_U (domWeilU hSiegelSet)) soFin_of; in the derivation of Theorem K the hypothesis hSiegelSet (GlobalTheory.Published.SiegelSetUnitary) is discharged by ThKR.siegel_of_core Prw.siegelCore_holds. weilConv_of uses the second clause of SoFin (every element of schA is a finite sum of pureA f phi with phi in SB) and dom_facts and dom_sum: integrability by Integrable.mono' with the bound p f * ht(h)^k * G, continuity by continuousAt_of_dominated, and the bound for a sum by exists_common, which adds the exponents of the summands (domWeil_of_U forgets that DomWeilU gives one exponent for all phi; the book keeps it). Relation to the literature: the convergence in (1) is Weil's convergence criterion for theta integrals [Wei65; KR88], Theorem lit-weil-siegel(2), in a different form. Weil's theorem is for the pair of B and the doubled space A^box of rank d = 2 rk A, with the condition that B is anisotropic or d/2 + r_B < rk B for the Witt index r_B; here W is any skew-Hermitian lattice space and the condition uses min(r, s), which bounds the Witt index of X, so the hypothesis is a special case of Weil's (min(r, s) = 0 makes X definite at every infinite place, hence anisotropic). The bound polynomial in ht(h) and the continuity in (2) go beyond absolute convergence; Weil's seminorm bound, Theorem lit-weil-siegel(1), is of the same kind as the domination of Lemma asm-theta-agree-convergence-dominated. Alpöge proves the lemma his own way, by the steps of the book.
asm-theta-agree-convergence-tori: EpsHerm (sigma(J_ji) = J_ij for all i, j, or = -J_ij, and det J ≠ 0), rId (u_t = 1 + realAd(e^t - 1)), Frame and Frame.IsGood (fields xx, yy, xy, aniso, add, cont, ax, ay, a0), Cone (antitone and nonnegative), rho2 (sum over i from 0 of (n - 2i - 1) t_i, which is delta_n with i from 1), SiegelCover, SiegelInt and TorHt (the Siegel properties (a), (b), (c)), sz with the embeddings B.emb, maj (with At (evI F) (z - c), 'z - c is at infinity'), latSum with S = Set.univ, posWt and coef (the integral of schr psi w Phi_1 times the conjugate of Phi_2). The Lean calls a Witt torus a Frame; the book keeps 'frame' for other objects. The Lean's sz, maj and latSum take any family of embeddings over the infinite places, and latSum a set S of rational matrices (also fullRank, the matrices of rank n, which this lemma does not use); the book uses the embeddings of a theta base and all rational matrices. The Siegel property (b) is stated for every Haar measure and fundamental domain, as SiegelInt is.
asm-theta-agree-convergence-siegel: (1) is GrpTop, proved by grpTop_of (lcsc_UA, RatUDiscrete.discreteTopology_ratU, continuous_ht). (2) is SiegelAll, which siegelAll_of derives from GlobalTheory.Published.SiegelSetUnitary, the Lean's statement of reduction theory for the unitary group of a nondegenerate Hermitian matrix and a Witt frame (IsWittFrame): an Iwasawa decomposition, a closed Siegel set covering the quotient by the rational points, the bounded conjugation of the parabolic part by the torus, the Siegel integration bound in multiplicative coordinates, the comparison of heights under rational elements, and rapid decay of cusp forms on the Siegel set. siegelAll_of rescales a skew-Hermitian J by sigma(x) - x (exists_herm_smul), takes a Witt frame (exists_isWittFrame, with 2q <= n from two_mul_le_of_wittFrame) and its torus (exists_torus), and passes in siegel_GAd to additive coordinates t = log u shifted by a constant (shf r c), in which the weight becomes exp(-[E:Q] delta_n(t)) (cone_integral_le, with [E:Q] = 2[F:Q]). Same as reduction theory for these groups [Bor69; BHC62], in the Lean's form; the rapid decay of cusp forms is not used here. In Theorem K, SiegelSetUnitary is proved by ThKR.siegel_of_core Prw.siegelCore_holds, Alpöge's own reduction theory.
asm-theta-agree-convergence-signature: EpsOf, proved by epsOf_of through SignatureOfHermitianForm.of_sig at one infinite place, with the scalar 1 for X.IsHerm and i for X.IsSkew (HasSig of c times J mapped by tau_w); the bound on the size of a Witt torus is sig_index, the bound for a totally isotropic subspace.
asm-theta-agree-convergence-theta: Part (1) is the first two clauses of GlobalTheory.T.theta_distribution_nonzero_admissible (CompanionTheory.ThetaAdm.theta_adm): summability of the theta sum on schA, and an l in (adeleClass F).adm with l = thetaSum on schA. Related to the continuity of Weil's theta distribution [Wei64]: admissibility asks only for continuity in the archimedean Schwartz component for each fixed finite component, and the Lean proves it its own way. Parts (2) and (3) are the clauses of ThK.ThetaBasic that this lemma uses, as thetaBasic_of proves them: continuity from hS.cont and the identity l = thetaSum after hS.pres, and continuity in f from hS.adm; additivity is theta_add (thetaSum_add after hS.pres). ThetaBasic also contains the invariance under rational elements (Lemma asm-theta-agree-anisotropic-automorphy) and a moderate growth bound, neither of which the convergence uses.
asm-theta-agree-convergence-poisson: CoefSum, proved by coefSum_of_annih annih (CoefSum.lean). The Poisson step is CS.Dual.poisson_le, applied with the dual pair dual (the characters u -> psi(u . xi), xi rational): for a continuous H whose translates by a compact set are bounded by a summable function, |sum H(xi)| <= mu(D)^(-1) sum_y |integral of e_y H|. The Lean proves it by Fourier series on the compact quotient (Stone-Weierstrass for the characters chiC, Dual.series), not from a published statement. It is a consequence of the Poisson summation formula [Tat67, Section 4.2] for the I-fold product, in a weaker form: an inequality, with no hypothesis on the Fourier coefficients. annih (RatOfKer: an adele a with psi(at) = 1 for all rational t is rational) is AdeleAnn.unitary_and_annihilator_eq.
asm-theta-agree-convergence-coefficients: (1) is CoefEq, proved by coefEq_of from the clause impl of the Weil representation (om(g,h) rho(w) = rho(mat g * w * (mat h)^T) om(g,h)) and inner_eq_of_unit (polarization, polar_int, with the clause unit). (2) is CoefBd, proved by coefBd_of from CoefReal through coef_split (the factorization along spl, with real_bound and fin_bound, and dual_cpt for the compactness in y) and sz_le; the Lean takes p = (1 + C L^N) p_0. CoefReal, proved by coefReal_of = RealFourierCoefficientBounds.main: for a Euclidean space V and N there is a continuous seminorm p on S(V) with |integral of e(2 pi i <u, y>) f_1(u + x) conj f_2(u) du| (1 + |x| + |y|)^N <= p(f_1) p(f_2). This is the continuity of the Fourier-Wigner transform from S(V) x S(V) to S(V x V) [Fol89, Chapter 1], which the Lean proves its own way.
asm-theta-agree-convergence-square: SqAll (SqBound for all Schwartz-Bruhat phi and S = Set.univ), proved by sqAll_of' coefSum coefEq_of (coefBd_of coefReal_of) through theta_mul_le (with the Haar measure ParityOfCoefficients.exists_haar), exists_ratEquiv (the bijection from hp.good.rat, injectivity of M.co.e and Module.finrank_matrix with [E:F] = 2) and sq_le_of_coef. The bound is in [0, infinity], where the lattice sum may be infinite.
asm-theta-agree-convergence-lattice: (1) LatInv, by latInv_of (latInvEquiv; the Lean also treats S = fullRank). (2) LatMeas, by latMeas (measurable_maj, isClosed_supp, continuous_mat_inv). (3) LatCpt, by latCpt_of (sz_mul_mul_le and LatticeQuotientCompactness.maj_le, with K = max(1, nd M M')^N). (4) LatArch, by latArch_of frameBasis_of (LatArchPf.torus and LatArchPf.maj_le, with C' = C). (5) LatTor, by latTor_of frameBasis_of oneVar_of, with N_0 = ([E:Q] + 1) nd: diag_coords gives m (denom_AE) and K_2 = max(1, sz(P) sz(Q)); tsum_oneMaj applies OneVar to the integer lattice of E in its Minkowski space, whose sup norm is at most the sum over the embeddings; tsum_fun_prod factors the sum; sum_pos_lam is the identity for P_{n,d}. The adapted basis is FrameBasis, by frameBasis_of (the x_i, the y_i and a basis of their orthogonal complement K). OneVar is oneVar_of from oneVar_core: the sum is compared with the integral of (1 + |y|)^(-N) over disjoint balls around the lattice points, then rescaled. In the Lean (1) to (4) hold for any family of embeddings and (3), (4) for any set S of rational matrices.
asm-theta-agree-convergence-cone: (1) is the first clause of PosWt, proved by Sq.posWt' through posWt_eq; PosWt also bounds the quantity viol, which is not used here. (2) is the first clause of ConeIntegralsFinite, proved by Sq.square_integrable_integral_holds through coneAff (with a = D(d/2 - n + 1), b = 2D) and ConeExp, cone_exponent_bound_holds: the integral of exp(sum c_i t_i) over the cone is finite when every partial sum of the c_i is negative, through ThetaSummability.Est.integrableOn_exp_logCone in the coordinates of the gaps. The second clause of ConeIntegralsFinite, for the cone of the second group, is not used.
asm-theta-agree-convergence-dominated: DomWeilU, proved by domWeilU hSiegelSet = domWeilU_of grpTop_of epsOf_of (siegelAll_of hSiegelSet) sqAll latInv_of latMeas latCpt_of (latArch_of frameBasis_of) latTor Sq.posWt' Sq.square_integrable_integral_holds. Step 1 is latSum_redH with exp_le_ht; it takes its own Siegel Witt torus of J_W from SiegelAll, and the Witt torus a' of Step 3 is the one of domWeilU_of, used only through LatTor at t = 0 (ha0: a'(0) = 1). G is latSum(g, 1)^(1/2) in [0, infinity], and the bounds are in the extended reals.
asm-theta-agree-continuity: ThK.SoCont, with pureA and sequences in SchwartzMap; like the lemma, it holds for Weil pairs of every signature. The proof is soCont hSiegelSet thetaBasic = soCont_of thetaBasic (domSoU hSiegelSet) soFin_of: dom_of_domSoU (Lemma asm-theta-agree-continuity-domination), the subspace soCoeff with a complement from Submodule.exists_isCompl and the projection linearProjOfIsCompl, the identity key (from the first clause of SoFin, Lemma asm-theta-agree-continuity-pieces(1)), and dom_sum and dom_facts (Lemma asm-theta-agree-continuity-integrals). Of ThetaBasic only the continuity clauses are used (Lemma asm-theta-agree-convergence-theta(2) and (3)); thetaBasic_of proves them from theta_distribution_nonzero_admissible and the clauses cont, pres and adm of the Weil representation. In Theorem K, hSiegelSet = ThKR.siegel_of_core Prw.siegelCore_holds.
asm-theta-agree-continuity-sums: (1) is latSum B.emb C N (fullRank E n d) g h, where fullRank E n d is the set of x with x.rank = n. (2) psum t i is the sum of the t_j with j < i (all of them when i exceeds the length of t), and viol s t is the supremum over i in Fin (q + 1) of psum s i - psum t i. (3) is fun x => Phi (-x), as in ThetaSumNeg.lean and HermitianFormDetNeZero.lean. (4) is soFin B M: phi in SB with pureA f phi in M.So B.psi B.tau_1 for every Schwartz function f.
asm-theta-agree-continuity-pieces: The first and fourth clauses of SoFin, proved by soFin_of. (1) uses sum_of_span with pf phi, the product over the finite places, which is Schwartz-Bruhat by pf_mem because phi_v = M.vac v = stdF for almost all v (hp.good.std). (2) uses exists_one (a Schwartz f_0 with f_0(0) = 1) and evaluation at finPt y; the constants are c_i f_i(0). SoFin also states that every element of schA is a finite sum of pure tensors with Schwartz-Bruhat finite parts, and that M.So is contained in schA; the lemma does not state these.
asm-theta-agree-continuity-cut-local: W.exists_cut, with the open subgroup of W.exists_dual (K is b/a times the integral matrices, with a from the compactness of the integral matrices). The Lean's hypotheses are a compact valuation subring O, that every neighbourhood of 0 has a nonzero element, a locally constant psi with psi(b) not 1, and characteristic 0; the lemma states the case of a nonarchimedean local field of characteristic 0, the case used (k = F_v). The set of full-rank matrices is open by isOpen_rank (rank_iff_det), and 2 Y_i is Y_0 + Y_0.
asm-theta-agree-continuity-eigen: W.coef_eigen, stated in the Lean for every function Phi with the Bochner integral, and for a character psi with |psi| = 1; the lemma states it for Schwartz-Bruhat Phi and the character of a theta base, the case used. The coefficient is coef F psi mu Phi (fun x => Phi (-x)) w.
asm-theta-agree-continuity-cut: SoCut, proved by soCut_of. The pieces chi_i are the preimages under iota (the clause bij of IsLinBar) of the functions g_i of exists_cut applied to iota phi; the test functions r are those of Rest (evFin F v_1). The element w is spM h t (-U) 0, the formula for <x, w> is sy (from ev_symp), the action of rho(w) at v is acts_schr, and the eigenvalue equation comes from the clause mult of IsLinBar at the points x = spM h t 0 (-(P^-1 Y (Q^T)^-1)) of coU, with P = t(J_X) and Q = t(J_W), invertible by det_X and hermitian_form_det_ne_zero. The vanishing is coef_eigen with M.co.form. The character psi_v is psv v psi, nontrivial by GaugeEx.CharLoc.char_local and locally constant by isLocallyConstant_addChar. The hypothesis on z is that z.map (piW (tau_1 comp sigma)) has rank different from n.
asm-theta-agree-continuity-fourier: FourierInj, proved by fourierInj_of through eq_zero, the injectivity of the Fourier transform on continuous integrable functions on A^kappa for the pairing psi(u . y), which the Lean proves for a standard character (with sch_props for continuity and integrability). The book cites Tate's self-duality of the adeles and Fourier inversion for it. The Lean states FourierInj for any number field and standard character; the lemma states it with the character of a theta base.
asm-theta-agree-continuity-parity: (1) is Parity, proved by parity_of coefEq_of fourierInj_of. The element is negOne sigma X.J, with mat = -1; coef_neg is the substitution x -> -x for the Haar measure of ParityOfCoefficients.exists_haar, which is invariant under negation. The Lean also treats the case in which every Schwartz-Bruhat function vanishes at every point, with c = 1; it does not occur. (2) is theta_neg, from Parity, thetaSum_neg and the commutation of g with negOne.
asm-theta-agree-continuity-square: SqSo (SqBound for soFin B M and S = fullRank E n d), proved by sqSo_of' soFin_of soCut_of (parity_of coefEq_of fourierInj_of) coefSum coefEq_of (coefBd_of coefReal_of). A map bounded by lattice sums is Qb B om N, with Qb.add, Qb.smul, qb_sum and latSum_mono. The decomposition is the fourth clause of SoFin with W.pure_update. The last step is qb_piece: theta_mul_le (Lemma asm-theta-agree-convergence-poisson, -coefficients(1) and the bijection exists_ratEquiv), theta_neg, CoefBd for phi and its reflection with P = compCLMOfContinuousLinearEquiv of negation, sq_le_of_coef, and the rank argument rank_of_mul and rank_of_map. The seminorm is sqrt(c) (p + p o P).
asm-theta-agree-continuity-full-sums: (1) is LatInv for S = fullRank E n d (latInvEquiv_rank). (2) is LatCpt, which latCpt_of proves for every S, applied to S = fullRank E n d. Lemma asm-theta-agree-convergence-lattice states both for S = Set.univ.
asm-theta-agree-continuity-minor: Minor, proved by minor_of frameBasis_of. The bases and linear forms are those of FrameBasis, the integers m (here Q) and K those of diag_coords; i maximizes psum s i - psum t i (exists_eq_ciSup_of_finite), the columns come from exists_cols_det_ne_zero, the embedding from exists_one_le_emb and norm_emb, the bound on the determinant is Matrix.det_le, and sum_lam_le_psum bounds the sum of the lambda'. The constant is c = (n! m K)^(-1).
asm-theta-agree-continuity-lattice: LatFull, proved by latFull_of latTor (minor_of frameBasis_of), with latTor = latTor_of frameBasis_of oneVar_of (Lemma asm-theta-agree-convergence-lattice(5)). N = N_0 + m(n + 1) and K = c^(-m(n + 1)) K_0, with m the integer called l in the lemma.
asm-theta-agree-continuity-decay: SoSemiU, proved by soSemiU hSiegelSet = soSemiU_of grpTop_of epsOf_of (siegelAll_of hSiegelSet) sqSo latInv_of latCpt_of latFull Sq.posWt'. The function ht-bar is qht (the infimum of ht over ratU; qht_le). A and k_1 are exp_le_ht, from TorHt of the Witt torus of W and the bound of GrpTop on compact sets; B_0 is the GrpTop bound on Omega. The exponent k = k_1 (m + D n), with m = D d + 2 k_0 N and D = finrank Q E, is chosen before phi, as in the Lean. The inequality S <= T + viol is the third clause of PosWt at i = q with psum_self and psum_le, and the bound on posWt is its first clause (Lemma asm-theta-agree-convergence-cone(1)). The Lean holds for every Weil pair, with no condition on the signature.
asm-theta-agree-continuity-volume: FinVolU, proved by finVolU: fv_exists_herm rescales a skew-Hermitian J to a Hermitian one with the same unitary group, and fundamental_domain_finite_volume reduces to GlobalTheory.CompanionTheory.SW.finVol_unitaryGroup, which the Lean proves (CompanionTheory.SWFin.finVol) for the unitary group of a nondegenerate Hermitian form. The published theorem is the finiteness of the volume of G(Q)\G(A_Q) for a reductive group G over Q without nontrivial rational characters; the restriction of scalars of U_J has none, and the Lean's statement is the special case of U_J with a fundamental domain for a Haar measure.
asm-theta-agree-continuity-domination: DomSoU (DomU M om (soFin B M)), proved by domSoU hSiegelSet = domSoU_of epsOf_of finVolU (soSemiU hSiegelSet): SoSemiU at N = 0, G = 1, setLIntegral_one, and FinVolU with hp.good.haar and hp.good.dom. dom_of_domSoU passes to Dom, the form used by dom_facts.
asm-theta-agree-continuity-integrals: dom_facts and dom_sum, for a set of finite parts satisfying Dom M om (a seminorm p, an exponent k and a function G for each phi); the lemma states the hypothesis for finitely many phi_i, each with its own k_i. Measurability comes from the first clause of ThetaBasic, integrability is Integrable.mono' with integrable_toReal_of_lintegral_ne_top, additivity is theta_sum, the common exponent is exists_common, and continuity in f is continuousAt_of_dominated with the fourth clause of ThetaBasic. Lemma asm-theta-agree-convergence uses the same two Lean theorems for all Schwartz-Bruhat phi in its range of signatures.
asm-theta-agree-density: ThKG.PolDense: Model.Pol is dense in SchwartzMap. It is proved by Dbl.polDense, which uses only the fields base, herm and skew of IsPair.
asm-theta-agree-density-moments: Dense.schwartz_functional_eq_zero_of_dense, for a finite-dimensional normed real space V; the Lean transports to EuclideanSpace by toEuclidean and works with polE of MvPolynomial in those coordinates. Its core is ThKOwn.eq_zero_PG and eq_zero_of_moments, for Q with Re Q(x) <= -w |x|^2; kill_mul needs the hypothesis WeakInt, proved as ThKOwn.weakInt.
asm-theta-agree-density-derivative: hasDerivAt_dOp (first claim, for every r with Rest) and actsD_unique (second claim), with dOp A B f = lineDeriv A f + (-2 pi i) linForm B f; the standard character enters through IsStd and phase_line.
asm-theta-agree-density-gaussian: Dense.exists_isGauss, which takes epsilon = 1 at every place. Q and Q' are pi T(c(-), -) and pi T(c'(-), -) for the trace form T = tr of DenseG; exists_isGauss does not record that they are symmetric.
asm-theta-agree-density-linear: fock_mul_linear, stated for any IsStd character; the operator is heisLine psi u with u = co.e.symm (0, b).
asm-theta-agree-partners: ThK.MatchEx, proved by matchEx_of from KCoinv through Partner.partner_of_big (part 1), partner_of_small (part 2) and match_of_polMatch (part 3), with polData_sum, finite_bad and Fam.sb.
asm-theta-agree-levi: LeviEx is the case t = 1 of Tow.Levi.exists_levi, which applies IsFr.levi (LeviAlg.lean) to the frame built from the adapted plane by isFrA: fr = (iota | x | y), gr J_1 = diag(J_1, ((0, 1), (-1, 0))), and m = fr diag(g, t, c(t)^-1) fr^-1.
asm-theta-agree-stabilizer: StabEx asks for some subgroup K with IsStab B K, compact, and Haar measures; IsStab determines K, and stabEx takes Stab.stabK. Compactness is isCompact_stabK, through cartan_bound, isCompact_latHat, vec_bound, fin_bound, exists_section, exists_compact_mat, isClosed_stabK and isCompact_of_units; the Haar measures are exists_haar_of_isCompact and exists_haar_idele.
asm-theta-agree-evaluation: ThK.EvZero, with X_1 = X and iota_X = 1. It and EvCone are the two parts of ThKF0.evaluation_at_zero_and_cone.
asm-theta-agree-evaluation-heisenberg: Five theorems of the Lean, each proved there (CompanionTheory.AdelicHeis.schr_mem_and_thetaSum, ThetaAdm.theta_adm, ThetaInj.theta_inj, ThetaUniq.theta_unique, AdelicSchur.schur), stated for a continuous character psi of the adeles of F, trivial on F and not 1: (1) theta_distribution_heisenberg_invariant, (2) theta_distribution_nonzero_admissible, (3) theta_heisenberg_translates_separate, (4) admissible_functional_rational_invariance, (5) heisenberg_commuting_operator_scalar. They are the standard facts on the Schroedinger representation of the adelic Heisenberg group and the theta distribution in [Wei64]: (5) is the irreducibility of the Schroedinger representation (Stone-von Neumann), (4) the uniqueness of the theta distribution up to a scalar among distributions invariant under the rational Heisenberg group, and (3) the injectivity of Phi -> (w -> theta(rho(w)Phi)). The Lean replaces tempered distributions by admissible forms, continuous in the archimedean Schwartz component for each fixed finite component, and states the rational invariance in (1) for every function, with its convention that a divergent sum is 0; the book states it on Schwartz-Bruhat functions, where it is used.
asm-theta-agree-evaluation-metaplectic: Mix.AdelSt, proved by Mix.adelic_estimates_holds = adelSt_of pure_tensor_estimates_holds finite_adelic_estimates_holds (infSt_of real_estimates_holds): at the real places Mix.Real.implSp writes the real symplectic map as a product of Fourier transforms, multiplications by chirps and linear changes of variables, at the finite places finite_adelic_estimates_holds uses local models (KCo.Mod.model), and adelSt_of glues them on pure tensors. Weil [Wei64] constructs, for s in Sp(A), an operator r(s) on S(A^kappa), defined up to a scalar, that intertwines rho(w) with rho(ws) and is the restricted tensor product of local operators, which for almost all v fix the characteristic function of O_v^kappa after normalization. An A-linear S preserving the standard form lies in Sp(A), as its matrix and that of its inverse are integral at almost all places. The Lean statement asks for the properties listed, with e_infinity a topological automorphism of the Schwartz space; unitarity is not part of it.
asm-theta-agree-evaluation-transfer: A transfer is ThKF0.Tw (fields maps, Heisenberg2, adm, ne) for Darboux coordinates d, d1 : Darboux B kappa of an A-module W with form B; rationally related is RatRel. (1) is tw_surj, with the metaplectic operator of AdelSt for d.e.symm.trans d1.e; (2) is Tw.theta and Tw.inj; (3) is Tw.exists_inv.
asm-theta-agree-evaluation-rational: ratRel_of_good gives RatRel M.co M1.co, the second sentence; exists_linearEquiv_of_rational is the dimension count, through Module.finrank_baseChange.
asm-theta-agree-evaluation-lattice: (1) is GlobalTheory.LatVacArith.psi_symp_latAtV, where symp(theta) is Tr(theta h); (2) is ThK.Vac.mem_latAtV, with the form symp(-1) of the model. The book gives both as computations with their Lean proofs, without a written proof.

asm-theta-agree-evaluation-adapted-commu: Lib.eq_zero_of_neg, for op a L = dop a L, the book's D_{a,L}; the proof is through l2Inner_op_right, op_comm and l2Inner_self_eq_integral_norm_sq for an additive Haar measure.
asm-theta-agree-evaluation-adapted-fock: Adp.map_eq, under the hypotheses Adp H eps Ma M1 (fields i, x, y, the three conditions on e^a) and B good, X Hermitian, W skew-Hermitian, H adapted; T, the book's R, is any linear map with T f y = f (glue eps 0 y). asm-theta-agree-evaluation-lagrangian: ThKF0.LagLine, proved by lagLine; the condition on L is that a is in L if and only if a.1 . b.2 = b.1 . a.2 for every b in L, and the invariance is under schr psi (t . emb w) for t in A and w in L. lagLine is LineCore.lagLine_of applied to realTest, and the proof follows it. The statement is the adelic form, for admissible forms, of the uniqueness up to a scalar of functionals on the Schroedinger representation invariant under a Lagrangian subgroup of the Heisenberg group; the book gives Alpoege's proof, place by place, since no published statement in this adelic form for admissible forms was located to cite. The local statements are those of Lemmas asm-theta-agree-evaluation-lagrangian-finite and asm-theta-agree-evaluation-lagrangian-real.
asm-theta-agree-evaluation-lagrangian-no: LagAlg.exists_mats, for any field F. The matrix P is the matrix of the first component of a section s of the first projection of L, and b = P^T beta.
asm-theta-agree-evaluation-lagrangian-fi: FinLine.test, for a commutative topological group G with NonarchimedeanAddGroup, a compact open subgroup U0, a set P with 0 in P and a linear form l on G -> C; SB G is the space of locally constant functions with compact support (tsupport). asm-theta-agree-evaluation-lagrangian-re: RealTest, proved by realTest: it gives f0 before quantifying over T, as here. The translation in (1) is g x = exp(2 pi i (b x p + b p p / 2)) f (x + p). asm-theta-agree-evaluation-unique: evaluation_at_zero_unique, through Geo.map_line lagLine with Geo.hasLagrangian_skew_adapted (via hasLag_of and exists_lag), evaluation_intertwining_of_models (GeoAdm.comp_mem_adm with proj_adm) and evaluation_intertwining_support (EvNonzero.exists_mem_schA_ev_ne_zero).
asm-theta-agree-tower-alpha: ThK.TowerA, with reG and CfgA; the character datum X is the same for all three triples. The proof follows ThKG.Tow.towerA_of planeEx modelEx ThKW.weilEx, as closeSph applies it: hP.1 (PlaneHerm) for G.V and hP.2 (PlaneSkew) for G.W at positions 0 and b + 1, with V'° = G.V' (reS G.V' G.V'); the triple for G° reuses the fields of hT (the models of reG keep co, vac, mu and dom, and Model.IsGood and Model.IsWeil involve only J and L); hM and hW give M_1, M'_1, om_1 and om'_1, with resEtaPow_of_add_two and resEtaPow_div for the restrictions of beta and beta/alpha; the inequalities are the omega goals of towerA_of. ThetaTowerProperties.lean has a second proof, GlobalTheory.ThK.towerA_of, from FunPr.Hypotheses_2 through KTowerPlane.exists_hyperbolic_split, PlaneSkew.plane_skew, ModelEx.model_exists and WeilExGen.exists_isWeil; closeSph does not use it.
asm-theta-agree-tower-isotropic: ThKG.Tow.Pln.exists_isotropic, which applies UTrans.exists_isotropic_of_indefinite to delta J, with delta = 1 if epsilon = 1 and c(delta) = -delta if epsilon = -1 (exists_skew), so that delta J is Hermitian. The Lean states it for any invertible epsilon-Hermitian J whose matrices kappa tau_w(J) have signature (r, s) with r, s >= 1, and proves it its own way: it diagonalizes the form (HermDiag.exists_congr_diagonal_herm) and represents -g_0 by the other diagonal entries (HermClass.exists_represent), with the local isotropy LocalQuad.isotropic_of_indefinite, which uses the Hasse norm theorem QNorm.hasseNormSt. The published route: after scaling by delta, x -> h(x, x) is a quadratic form over F in 2n >= 6 variables whose isotropic vectors are those of h; it is isotropic at every finite place [OMe63, 63:19] and indefinite at every real place, so it is isotropic by the Hasse-Minkowski theorem [OMe63, Section 66]. Landherr's theorem [Lan36] gives the same through the classification of Hermitian forms.
asm-theta-agree-tower-pair: ThKG.Tow.Pln.exists_adapted_pair, stated in the Lean for any O_E-submodule D of E containing 1 whose elements are integral at every tau_v; exists_plane applies it with D = intE (Hermitian) and D = codE (skew-Hermitian), the integrality being val_le_one_of_intE and val_le_one_of_codE (through val_le_one_of_codiff, psi_int and the field psiP of Base.IsGood). The vector z_0 is exists_max_val, over the primes splitPrime (tau_v) and splitPrime (tau_v o sigma); the partner is exists_partner, with the fractional ideal C = h(L, x) and the criterion crit; the element d is exists_denom. theta is passed to exists_adapted_pair by exists_plane, which takes it from exists_integer_add_conj_eq_one_of_formallyUnramified and the field unram of Base.IsGood.
asm-theta-agree-tower-cartan: ThKG.Tow.Pln.real_plane, which assumes a left inverse P of iota in place of independent columns. The Cartan involution A Delta A^{-1} is cartan_of_frame (with frame_inv), and the comparison of signatures is hasSig_unique, through Formalism.UG.P.sig_dim, with hasSig_exists for M_1. exists_plane applies it with M = kappa tau_w(J), X = tau_w(x) and Y = kappa tau_w(y).
asm-theta-agree-tower-basis: ThKG.Tow.Pln.exists_basis; the completion is AdelicU.splitLat and beta O_v^n = L_tau is IsSplitBasis. The inclusions are map_mem_splitLat, splitLat_le and map_mem_of_unit; the columns other than i_0 and i_1 are placed by skip i_0 i_1.
asm-theta-agree-tower-plane: ThKG.Tow.PlaneHerm and PlaneSkew, whose conjunction is PlaneEx, proved by planeHerm and planeSkew as Pln.exists_plane with (epsilon, kappa, D) = (1, 1, intE) and (-1, i, codE), through isHerm_iff and isSkew_iff (IsEps). asm-theta-agree-tower-eigen: Tw.VacLoc.exists_schr_eigen, with A = (M -> O_v) for a finite type M. Step 1 is GlobalTheory.T.continuous_character_cocycle_trivial_near_zero (CocycleChar.cocycle_char_trivial_near_zero); Step 2 is Tw.SchrTestVec.exists_fixed (exists_fixed_of_subgroup with the subgroup O_v^I); Step 3 is Tw.SympDualNbhd.exists_dual_nbhd; the character sum is exists_twisted_sum_ne_zero and the averaging is avg_fixed; the commutation rule is schr_comm, and Tw.SchrSBFin.schr_mem_SB keeps the Schwartz-Bruhat functions.
asm-theta-agree-tower-cocycle: (1) is Tw.LatParam.latAtV_param, with Gamma_v = latAtV X W v; (2) is Tw.LatVacArith.psi_symp_latAtV, through psi_gen, trace_int_of_lat and psi_int (GlobalTheory.IntDense.addChar_eq_one_of_integral); (3) is Tw.VacCocycle.psi_half_symp_add, with symp_swap. Tr h(xi gamma, gamma') is symp (cA sigma) xi, and the symplectic form is symp (cA sigma) (-1).
asm-theta-agree-tower-vacuum: (1) is Tw.VacAny.exists_isVac_any_darboux, through latAtV_param, psi_half_symp_add, exists_schr_eigen and Tw.SchrLoc.schr_tens_of_at; (2) is Tw.VacIndic.eventually_isVac_indicator, which is isVac_indicator_of_theta, through exists_gen, eventually_psiLoc_eq_one, eventually_int and acts_indicator. asm-theta-agree-tower-model: ThKG.Tow.ModelEx, proved by modelEx. The coordinates are Tw.RatDarboux.exists_rational_darboux_of_isGood = exists_rational_darboux (exists_darboux, with GlobalTheory.exists_isSymplecticBasis_of_finrank, isAlt_sympBil, bijective_sympBil and symp_map for the extension of scalars); the measure and the domain come from ThKF.unimodularity_holds (unimodLC, countable_ratU, discrete_ratU and RationalUnitaryDomains.isDiscreteWithDomains_of_discrete); the vacua are those of Lemma asm-theta-agree-tower-vacuum, chosen with if-then-else as in the proof.
asm-theta-agree-tower-weil: ThKG.Tow.WeilEx. Its statement is that of GlobalTheory.Published.WeilRepresentationExists, the field weilRepresentationExists of Theorem lit-bundle-theta (FunPr.ThetaLocalInputs). The route of closeSph proves it its own way as ThKW.weilEx = ThKW.S.exists_isWeil: from a Weil datum for the Hermitian matrices -xi_0 J_W^{-1} and J_X^T, with c(xi_0) = -xi_0 (exists_isWeilDatumOF), carried to the model by exists_isUWeilPair_cm. asm-theta-agree-tower-beta: ThK.TowerB, with reG and CfgB. The proof follows ThKG.Tow.towerB_of planeEx modelEx ThKW.weilEx, as closeSph applies it: hP.1 (PlaneHerm) for G.V' at positions 0 and b + 1 and hP.2 (PlaneSkew) for G.W at positions a and a + b + 1, with V° = G.V; resEtaPow_of_add_two gives the restriction of alpha.
