asm-theta-agree-split: ThK.SplitEx; uniqueness is ExistsUnique of the pair. The proof is splitEx_of, the second component of ct_all, with TriplePair, Low, PairEx, EvZero, anyBig, anySmall and split_uniq.
asm-theta-agree-split-notions: IsoV is the subtype of nonzero x in E^n with form x x = 0, with the action isoAct of the units of E; Moves H gamma, Iwa H K, KFinite om K Phi and coneI. Moves and Iwa take a plane H and use only H.x; the book states them for a vector. coneI is the function of h_1 whose value at 1 the Lean's ConeA and ConeB compare with the integral of the sum over isotropic vectors. As in the Lean, the integrals are Bochner integrals, so the integral of a function that is not integrable is 0.
asm-theta-agree-split-low: Low, proved by low_of = low_eps applied to the frame isFr (the basis (iota, x, y) with a left inverse whose first block is P). The signature is real_plane (Lemma asm-theta-agree-tower-cartan), the Cartan involution cartan_low, the lattice isLattice_comap with hH.split for the dual, and the basis at the places of P splitLat_map with the matrix T that skips the positions i_0 and i_1.
asm-theta-agree-split-witt: Witt, proved by witt_of. (1) is aniso at one infinite place. For (2) the Lean multiplies J by an element c with sigma(c) = -c (ThKF.exists_scale) to obtain a skew-Hermitian matrix with the same unitary group and isotropic vectors, and applies ThKEnd.Grp.wittVec, whose witt_step is the transvection v -> v + b^{-1} h(v, x - x') (x - x'); the book writes the same transvections for the Hermitian form. Tow.Levi.exists_UA puts the matrix in U_X(F). This is the case of one isotropic vector of Witt's extension theorem.
asm-theta-agree-split-inputs: Fields of the record behind ct_all, each stated as its Prop: (1) UnipEx without its last clause (an idele of absolute value > 1), and StabDec; (2) KFinData; (3) IwaEx, which the Lean states for any plane H with H.x nonzero and isotropic; the proofs of (1), (3) and the first claim of (2) follow unipEx_of and stabDec_of, iwaEx_of (IwaG.iwa_glob with Iwa.iwaLoc) and the first component of kFinData_of; (1)(a) and (b) are the Lean's unipGood for J Hermitian or skew-Hermitian, which the book cites as Lemma asm-theta-agree-end-unipotent through its proof; (4) MixW; (5) MixAB with Mix2; (6) SoStab, stated for all Weil pairs; Lemma asm-theta-agree-coinvariants-inputs(4) is its case of the second pair of a triple; (7) SoEv and SoZeroA'; (8) TwoExp; (9) the three ingredients of ctKernel_of: (a) Ker.sum0 with the constant of (pol0 ..).exp (ThetaExp), the integral being the Lean's tm integrated over a fundamental domain, (b) Ker.constant_term_anisotropic_integral_zero, (c) Ker.constant_term_cone_integral_eq with the constant C * c from (polX ..).exp and (polA ..).uniq; (10) ConeA; (11) ConeB; (12) MixX (ThKG.MixX, proved by Mix.mixX_closed), another field of the record, which Ker.mixAB_of, soZeroA'_of and ctKernel_of use; the book adds it as a part so that the proofs of (5) and (9)(c) can cite it. The absolute convergence of the sums is Summable for complex-valued functions on countable sets. MixW is shared with Lemma asm-theta-agree-evaluation through adelic_estimates_holds. In (9)(c) the Lean takes the constants C and c from one fixed Weil pair and uses them for all; the book does the same. The proof of (3) argues integrality at almost every place through generators of the lattice, as ae_mulVec does. The proofs of (10) and (11) follow coneA_of and coneB_of through cone_core: the rules (L) and (T) are the fields torW and tor of the Lean's record Laws (lawsA, lawsB), and the Lean takes kappa from Unfold for one fixed pair of Weil pairs, as the book does. The proof of (4) is the factorization in mixW_of_adel into the laws Chr.lawW_left, lawW_unip and lawW_levi, which are (4a), (4b) and (4c); that of (12) is the factorization in mixed_model_plane_X_m into adapted_plane_pair_local_factor, adapted_plane_pair_theta_integral and adapted_plane_pair_seesaw_identity, which are (12a), (12b) and (12c); (12b) is MixXUnip.unip_trivial_m. The proofs of (4a), (4b), (4c), (12a) and (12c) follow lawW_left, lawW_unip, lawW_levi, e_om_one_eq_om1_one_e and mixX_levi, which apply TA', TU, TB, TA' and TB (Proposition asm-theta-agree-split-inputs-seesaw) with the charts of setW and setX; the existence in (12) is exists_isEv_mixedX_m (Lemma asm-theta-agree-split-inputs-xexists).
asm-theta-agree-split-inputs-heis: IsSp, IsImp, Rel, Law, IsE, Cyc, boxFun, dv and dbS (ResAdm.lean, SchrodingerApplyZeroOfFst.lean, BoxCancel.lean). The Lean states them for an abstract test class C over a ring R, with a space sp of test functions, a set adm of admissible forms and a modulus modu; the book states them for the class adeleClass F of Schwartz-Bruhat functions and admissible forms on powers of the adeles, the only class the laws of Lemma asm-theta-agree-split-inputs use. An (S,j)-evaluation is the Lean's IsE, and lying over is Rel.
asm-theta-agree-split-inputs-heis-axioms: The axioms Ax (AxB with AxDelta and AxImp) and AxInt for adeleClass F: ax_of (axB, axDelta_of lagLine, axImp_of adelic_estimates_holds) and axInt. asm-theta-agree-split-inputs-heis-lines: Ax.schur, Ax.line, IsImp.cyc and Ax.cyc, Ax.exists_form, IsImp.law_res, Ax.isE_res and Ax.exists_E, Ax.E_cyc, Ax.comp_cyc and Ax.comp_ne, and Ax.uniq (SchrodingerApplyZeroOfFst.lean), which the Lean proves for any test class satisfying Ax. The facts (L1) and (L2) are Law.apply and Law.inv.
asm-theta-agree-split-inputs-heis-double: IsSp.dbS, rel_dv and schr_dv, Ax.box_E, Ax.box_ne, Ax.exists_diag and Ax.exists_avg (BoxCancel.lean). The maps K of (4) and K' of (5) are the Lean's kE for the predicate true and for membership in the image of j; the form I of (5) is the AxInt form for the complement of j, made cyclic through fE. In Ax.exists_avg the automorphism g is an R-linear equivalence of the functions on the complement and the factor is C.modu (det g).
asm-theta-agree-split-inputs-heis-scalar: (1) is the common first step of lev_scalar (ExistsDoubledUnitaryBlock.lean), lev_scalar2 (LevScalar2.lean) and Ax.exists_char (DetConjMulVec.lean): e' = om1(g^-1) . e . om(m) is made proportional to e by Ax.uniq. asm-theta-agree-split-inputs-side: IsUWeilB (HilbertNinetyQuotientHomEqIff.lean), with IsUSplitting, IsDblCoord, IsUWeilSplit and SiegelRule. The Lean's Darboux chart may have any finite index set, as here. IsUWeilB also asks that the operators preserve L2 norms and that the diagonal be a Lagrangian (IsLagr); Proposition asm-theta-agree-split-inputs-seesaw does not use these, and they are left out. The Lean's omd is a homomorphism of groups, as is the representation of (b) here. A Weil pair's IsWeil is IsUWeilPair, whose two components, with the transposed chart d' satisfying d'.e(x^T) = M.co.e(x), are the two Weil sides of the last sentence.
asm-theta-agree-split-inputs-siegel: parabolic_character_trivial_on_diagonal (DoubledUnitaryCharacterTrivialOfSiegel.lean), stated for J over E with sigma(J_ji) = eps J_ij and det J nonzero, and for continuous homomorphisms into the units of C. Step 2 is local_global_character_interpolation (the element piece and tendsto_mix'); Step 1 is triv_piece, through hermitian_darboux_split_product, which is CellSplit.char_trivial_first (HermitianDarbouxSplitProduct.lean) for the splitting of A tensor E given by splitS. char_trivial_first applies char_trivial_artinian (FiniteNonunitMatrix.lean, Lemma asm-theta-agree-split-inputs-siegel-artinian) to the Artinian ring R_S tensor E, the matrix dbl J and the diagonal Lagrangian diagCols (isLagr_diagCols).
asm-theta-agree-split-inputs-siegel-situ: The data shared by SiegelChar.lower_triv and cell_triv (section Abstract of SplitQuadraticAlgebraOrder.lean) and Ar.RT.Siegel.triv_of_cell (FiniteNonunitMatrix.lean): R an E-algebra, c : E -> E, sigma an additive map R ->+ R with h1 : sigma 1 = 1, phi : G ->* R, lam : G ->* units of C, and e, f with hef, hee, hff, hef0, hfe0. Each lemma adds its own hypotheses on sigma, phi and c.

asm-theta-agree-split-inputs-siegel-cell: SiegelChar.cell_triv; hypothesis (1) is hlow, (2) is hP, and the condition sigma(phi g) phi g = 1 is hu.
asm-theta-agree-split-inputs-siegel-fini: Ar.RT.Siegel.finite_nonunit_matrix, through finite_nonunit for the polynomial det(A + X B + X^2 D) over E. SplitQuadraticAlgebraOrder.lean has variants of both, and of triv_of_cell, for E finite over F; the Artinian versions are the ones used.
asm-theta-agree-split-inputs-siegel-gene: Ar.RT.Siegel.triv_of_cell (FiniteNonunitMatrix.lean). The Lean takes an infinite field F with E Artinian, c an F-algebra map, R = Matrix beta beta E, the image condition as hu and hsurj, h2 that 2 is a unit, hξ and hc for xi, and hcell; y, y' and the three finite sets f1, f2, f3 are as in the proof.

asm-theta-agree-invariance-poisson: ThetaUniq.comb_of_basis, which transports DiracComb.eq_mul_comb (for R^n with the standard lattice) along the coordinates of the basis. Relation to the literature: the classical description of the tempered distributions invariant under a lattice and under the characters dual to it, a consequence of Poisson summation and of the Fourier expansion of periodic distributions [Hor90, Section 7.2]: such a T is periodic, so T is the sum of c_k exp(2 pi i <k, x>); invariance under the characters makes c_k constant; and the sum of the exp(2 pi i <k, x>) is the Dirac comb by Poisson summation. The Lean proves it directly: T vanishes on functions supported in the unit ball that vanish at 0, by Hadamard's lemma f = sum_i (exp(2 pi i x_i) - 1) g_i (exists_div); so T(f) = T(b) f(0) there for a bump function b; translation by the lattice gives T(f) = T(b) sum_m f(m) for f of compact support (exists_partition), and density of these in the Schwartz space (dense_hasCompactSupport) concludes.

asm-theta-agree-invariance-doubling: seesaw_theta_dual_pair, proved by ThetaMember.theta_om_rational through split_of_eq (which is weil_representation_theta_equivariance) for dbl J_B (isHerm_dbl) with the Lagrangian diagCols (isLagr_diagCols, with C_x = (1, -1) and the inverse (1/2)(1 1; 1 -1)), the rational coordinates dblCoord d_0, the element exists_dbl_elem, the box compatibility of IsWeilB, theta_sum_tensor_product, and the function of theta_adm with nonzero theta sum.
asm-theta-agree-invariance-rational: theta_sum_rational_invariance, through darboux_coordinates_rational_exist. Step 1 is hP.herm.sig, hP.skew.sig, rat_det_ne_zero_of_hasSig and rat_det_ne_zero_of_map; Step 2 is exists_isQuad; Steps 3 to 5 are Resc.member (isWeilB_resc for the rescaling, with ug_smul and symp_smul; exists_ratCoord for the rational coordinates; then seesaw_theta_dual_pair), applied first to om composed with inr (hB, a = 1, b = -delta^{-1}) and then to om composed with inl (hA, a = -delta^{-1}, b = 1); Step 6 is the identity e. Relation to the literature: Weil [Wei64, Chapitre III, n. 41, formula (39) and Théorème 6] proves that the sum of Phi over X_k equals that of r_k(s) Phi for s in the rational pseudo-symplectic group, with his lift r_k to the metaplectic group; this is an instance of Théorème 4 of Chapitre I, n. 19, which contains Poisson summation as the case of an isomorphism exchanging a lattice and its dual. Here the operators omega(gamma, gamma') are any operators that satisfy the axioms of a Weil representation (Definition asm-theta-agree-models(6)): they normalize the Schrödinger operators as the rational symplectic elements do, so they agree with Weil's operators up to scalars (Weil's Théorème 1, Chapitre I, n. 10, for unitary operators), and the Siegel rules of the axioms are what make the scalars 1. The Lean does not use Weil's theorem: it gets the invariance up to a scalar from Lemma asm-theta-agree-invariance-unique, which rests on Poisson summation in the form of Theorem asm-theta-agree-invariance-poisson, and shows that the scalar is 1 by Lemmas asm-theta-agree-invariance-split and asm-theta-agree-invariance-character.
asm-theta-agree-anisotropic-invariance: ILeft, proved by iLeft thetaBasic as I_left unimodularity_holds. The theta integral Model.I is a Bochner integral, and in Mathlib the Bochner integral of a function that is not integrable (or not almost everywhere strongly measurable) is 0 by definition. ILeft and I_left state the equality for every Phi in schA with this convention, and so does the lemma, which says the convention explicitly. The integral identity is L2.integral_right: the change of variables setIntegral_image_emb for right translation by g_0 (measurePreserving_mul_right), fd_right, and IsFundamentalDomain.setIntegral_eq, which holds for every function invariant under ratU because integrability passes between fundamental domains and both integrals are 0 otherwise. The proof in the book spells out that transfer; the same transfer for right translation is L2.integrableOn_right. Unimod gives the countability of ratU, a Haar measure with a fundamental domain, and the right invariance of every Haar measure; unimodularity_holds proves it through unimodLC, which rests on AdelicStabUnimod.unimodularOver_adele.

asm-theta-agree-rechoice: ThK.PolRe, proved by polRe_of2T (GlobalTheory.CompanionTheory.ThetaK, restated as HoweDualityUnitaryAlt.polRe_of2T) from JoinTri, MaxFinT, ArchOp, ArchLie, ArchUniq, PolCount, CartanConj, CartanMove, KCoinv and ILeft; its proof is followed. The constant is c_2 * (c * prod over v in X.T of c_v). The older proof polRe_of takes Published.HoweDualityReal and MaxFin in place of JoinTri and MaxFinT; the closing of Theorem K uses polRe_of2T.

(2) is Published.ThetaSubInf. (3) is Published.ThetaSub, with augAt om v. (4) is ThKF.Moves; in the Lean the second space is reS Y Y2, with the matrix and lattice of Y.

asm-theta-agree-rechoice-operators: (1) is the first clause of ArchOp, proved by A.archOp through A.exists_op: Step 2 is exists_lin (apply_pure, exists_char_ne, exists_schwartz_slice) with phB_fin for Step 1; Step 3 is impl_of, surj_of and E.Impl.continuous (Impl.dRho, weylAlg_induction and RealWeil.exists_seminorm_le, which the Lean proves and the book cites as Sobolev's inequality); Step 4 is acts_of. asm-theta-agree-rechoice-intertwine: (1) is hD1 in cartanMove_of, from RL.derEx (Lemma asm-theta-agree-real-derivative) and RL.actsLaws (Lemma asm-theta-agree-real-weak). (2) is Cart.intertw.
asm-theta-agree-rechoice-fock: The first part is Cart.pol_le as applied in cartanMove_of (a = mat g^-1, b = mat h^-1, with intertw). The second part is the clause of ArchOp for K_inf, which A.archOp proves as A.map_Pol with X2 = X and W2 = W; map_Pol derives the same intertwining identity from T_D (Impl.dRho), and the book uses Lemma asm-theta-agree-rechoice-intertwine(2) for both.
asm-theta-agree-rechoice-lie: ArchLie, a hypothesis of closeSph, discharged in theoremK_head2_of_mod by archLie' localLift_holds; the proof of archLie' through lie' is followed: exists_sp (Step 2), LocalLift (Step 3), Impl.scalar (Step 4), exists_smooth_fun (Step 5), weylAlg_induction with D_mem_Pol and actsD_of (Step 6). LocalLift, the local metaplectic lift with derivative quad X + c at 0, is proved in the Lean as localLift_holds; it is part (2) of Lemma asm-theta-agree-real-metaplectic, which cites the metaplectic representation [Wei64], [Fol89]. The coordinates of Step 3 are the Lean's Coord (nonempty_coord). Another proof, archLie_of, assumes Published.RealMetaplecticRepresentation. In the proof of Lemma asm-theta-agree-rechoice the lemma is used only with one of the two lines trivial.
asm-theta-agree-rechoice-count: PolCount, proved by polCount_of_derEx = PC.polCount_of (RL.fockEx derEx) (RL.vacLine derEx). The Lean shows that Pol(M) lies in the range of the Fock map (PC.pol_le, through VacLine) and bounds the rank of the tensor product of polynomial rings (rank_tens); the book uses Lemma asm-theta-agree-real-fock-map(2), whose image statement contains that inclusion. The frames come from RL.frameEx (Lemma asm-theta-agree-real-frames), as in exists_fock.
asm-theta-agree-rechoice-linear: (1) is pol_lie, (2) is pol_k, and (3) is exists_linop (with rinf_ex for the uniqueness). The uniqueness is ArchUniq, proved by A.archUniq; it is the uniqueness of Lemma asm-theta-agree-real-weak(3).
asm-theta-agree-rechoice-howe: (1) is ThKF.inf_uniq2 with JoinAt, a field of JoinTri; closeSph obtains JoinTri as Join.joinTri_of from FockEx, PolRange, LieFirst and LieSecond. JoinAt for a pair is part (2) of Theorem lit-howe-duality-real, which the book cites; the older inf_uniq applies Published.HoweDualityReal directly. (2) is MaxAt for the pair, from MaxFinT = Sph.maxFinT_of SphTri, whose proof (locRep_tri, maxAt_of, thetaSub_sup, Stab.sup_ne, Stab.not_mem) is followed; SphTri is Theorem th-howe-finite, passed to closeSph as sphTri_of.
asm-theta-agree-rechoice-kernels: (1) is maxInfP, through absMax (Steps 1 and 2) and max_inf with maximal_of (Step 3). (2) is maxFinP, through absMax and max_fin, with ex_fin for the actions at v.
asm-theta-agree-rechoice-compare: (1) is archimedean_matched_maps_compare; the Lean states it for two matched quadruples with the same finite maps and uses only their triple and real maps. (2) is cmp_finT, whose hypotheses on Rf_2 (nontriv, onto, onto', maxFinP for the second quadruple, equiv) come from the second matched quadruple; c_v = 1 for v not in X.T is cf1 in polRe_of2T.
asm-theta-agree-rechoice-cartan: CartanConj, proved by cartan_conjugacy_holds = Cart.exists_conj with c = i; cartanMove_of uses exists_conj with c = 1 for the Hermitian space. The Lean states it for W and reS W W2. The frames are RL.frameEx (Lemma asm-theta-agree-real-frames) through conj_mat and frame_inv, and g is built by exists_point.
asm-theta-agree-rechoice-move: CartanMove, proved by cartanMove_of ArchOp; its proof is followed. The Lean states it for a model M2 of (reS X X2, reS W W2) with M2.co = M.co and both pairs of the same signature.
asm-theta-agree-rechoice-transport: ThKF.real_trans: quot_trans gives (a) with conj_line, cj1, Moves.up and transK; (b) is r.lie and r.cpt with transL, transK and cj2; (c) uses pol_lie, pol_k, cj3, Moves.down and ArchUniq. Step 1 is transL. The Lean assumes triples for G and G-circ and real maps for G.
asm-theta-agree-nonvanishing: ThK.NonZeroAn. G.p = 0 means that V is definite, and G.q = 0 that V' is. Only the part for G.q = 0 is used in the derivation. Proved by Dbl.nonZeroAn_of NonZeroBot TowerA TowerB EvZero CTBigZero CTSmallZero SchToPol PolSch LeviEx SplitEx ToSo (NonZero.lean): big_of is the induction on q for G.p = 0 and small_of the induction on p for G.q = 0; both pass from G to the re-chosen datum reG G V V' W, whose models are those of G but whose PolData (through the Gaussians, which use the theta_w) may differ, and SchToPol bridges the two. The contradiction uses Split2 of the zero function and C != 0 at h = 1, where om (1, 1) Phi = Phi.
asm-theta-agree-nonvanishing-schwartz: Dbl.PolSch (polSch) and Dbl.SchToPol (schToPol_of WeilConv). The span of pure tensors pure f phi with Dense.Good phi (local Schwartz-Bruhat components, almost all the indicator stdF) contains schA by Dense.schA_le; on each, f -> I(pure f phi)(h) is a continuous linear functional by I_add and the second clause of WeilConv, and Dense.pol_dense kills it. The regularity field std of Model.IsGood gives phi_v = vac_v for almost all v.
asm-theta-agree-nonvanishing-full-rank: Dbl.ToSo, proved by toSo_of KReal KFin KCoinv ThetaBasic CptAll (ConvOfCpt.lean). CptAll (cptAll_of GrpTop EpsOf SiegelAll FinVolU Unimod) is Lemma asm-theta-agree-definite-compact; conv_of_cpt bounds the theta function by Cpt.bdd. conv_of_cpt gives convergence from ThetaBasic and Cpt, I_lin the linearity, pol_sch the inclusion of PolData in schA, and I_aug the replacement at v_1; I_aug is proved from I_lin and I_act like Lemma asm-theta-agree-anisotropic-augmentation (kill_aug), which the book cites. The data at v_1 are the second and third clauses of Coinv at B.v_1, which is clean by Chars.IsGood.
asm-theta-agree-nonvanishing-doubling: IsStab2, IsEmb, locGrp, IntAt, OffAt and IsSphAt are defined for every lattice space Y : Spc F E n, with no Hermitian or skew-Hermitian condition, and the book states (1) and (2) in the same generality; the lemmas that use K add the condition (Lemma asm-theta-agree-doubling-stabilizer, for Hermitian or skew-Hermitian spaces). K is Dbl.IsStab2 (an iff, so K is determined); iota is IsEmb, realized by Hgt.emb2. The matrix coefficient is coef (an integral against a Haar measure nu on A^I), the zeta integrand zint = (a(e(g,1)) : C)^(s - (d - n)/2) * coef. U^(v) is locGrp (the subgroup generated by UAt, the elements at v), integral at v is IntAt, trivial at v is OffAt, Omega_T is {g | forall v not in T, IntAt v g}, spherical at v is IsSphAt (p with IsPar p t and mat2 p - 1 at v, k in K with mat2 k - 1 at v). d_v is locD E n v (the sign is 1 when Nonempty (E ->_F F_v)), L_v is LFun.Lv (charFam chi) v (Euler factors locL over the places above v, trivial where chi is ramified), and L(s, chi) is charL chi with the empty set of excluded places.
asm-theta-agree-nonvanishing-zeta: Four hypotheses of nonZeroBottom_of_doubling_integral, as pair_ne_zero uses them. (1) HgtEx, discharged by hgtEx = hgtEx_of stab2Cpt; it holds for every Hermitian or skew-Hermitian lattice space and also gives the continuous embedding e = emb2, which is iota. (2) RealInv, by realInv_of ArchOp; its hypothesis RealQuot is condition (a) of the real maps. (3) NormZeta, by normZeta_of SWFullX BoxSecX DblX HgtEx HgtInt Stab2Cpt CptAll ThetaBasic PolSch; it holds for every K, a and e with IsStab2, IsHgt and IsEmb, and is the only part that uses EisBL and SiegelWeilStd (through SWFullX). (4) BadFactor, by badFactor; it also holds for every such K, a and e. The book states (1) and (2) under min(r, s) = 0, the case it uses.
asm-theta-agree-nonvanishing-zeta-local: (1) is Bump (bump), stated for an IsPair with n <= d and v in B.P; the elements g at v are UAt X (evFin v), integral at v is IntAt, and acts at v is Acts (evFin v). (2) is VacFix2 (vacFix2), stated for any doubling coordinates IsDblCoordX and doubled Weil operators IsUWeilSplit with a Hecke character unramified above v; the book states it for the doubling datum of Lemma asm-theta-agree-doubling-datum(2), the case badFactor_of uses. The proof of (1) follows bump; the topological Step 1 combines near_UA, near_units and exists_level, which the Lean applies to transposed matrices. The proof of (2) follows vacFix2: the blocks of k and k^-1 lie in Pres v X by presD_of and pres_of_hat, the eigenvectors come from Vf.dbl_eigen (Lemma asm-theta-agree-local-vacuum-doubled) applied to the splitting of IsUWeilSplit, the decomposition is Vf2.exists_beta and Vf2.exists_decomp, the Siegel rule is rule_diag, chi_W(det t) = 1 is chi_det, and |c| = 1 is Bad.norm_eig, from the unitarity of the doubled operators (IsUnitaryOn) rather than from the compactness of K as in Lemma asm-theta-agree-local-factor-vacuum.
asm-theta-agree-nonvanishing-zeta-local-: Vf2.exists_skew (SkewTwo.lean), for a commutative ring A with a ring endomorphism c with c(c z) = z, a surjection r onto a field with the dichotomy hcase and the unit criterion hu, and G with a right inverse G'. The step is Vf2.step, the rank increase Vf2.rank_lt and the skew matrices Vf2.skew_two; the induction runs up to Fintype.card + 1 steps.

Vf2.exists_beta (CompCA.lean), for g in UG (cA sigma) (dbl (incM F X.J)) with g * diagCols = fromRows x y; preserving L_v is membership in Pres v X, and b^T J = J c(b') is Adj (cA sigma) (incM F X.J) b b'. The residue map is Vf2.exists_res (KFinLoc.split_or_inert), the frame a is bc iota P for P from AdelicU.Frames.exists_rational_frame with Vf2.fr_iff, the Gram matrix is integral with integral inverse by Hgt.gram_loc (from the duality hX.dual, with delta = 1), the isotropy relation is Vf2.lag_of, and the inverse is Vf.exists_inv.

Vf2.exists_decomp (SkewTwo.lean), for an R-algebra A with c an R-algebra map, the elements s, n and p of UG c (dbl J) and t in GL with t^-1 = t'. C, C^-1 and S are CC b, Ci b and SS eps, and the conjugation by C is mkU; the Lean states the formulas for s, n_0 and n_0^-1 and the equalities t = y + b(y - x) and t^-1 = t'. It generalizes Vf.exists_decomp of Lemma asm-theta-agree-local-vacuum-decomposition, which is the case x = k, y = 1 with T built from (1 + (1 - k) b) f' = 1.

Bmp.keep is (1); Bmp.dich is (2), stated for a principal ideal domain O with fraction field K that is local, with the condition on psi as the hypothesis hpsi, a in the maximal ideal and nonzero, and lam K a n d = a M_{n x d}(O). bump applies it with O the integers of F_v, psi = psiV B.psi v, y the first n rows of the identity of size d, and h = (invT g0)^{-1}, the transpose of g0. Bmp.sep is the separation of a vector from a lattice used in the second case.
asm-theta-agree-doubling-iwasawa: Hgt.hasIwasawa_fin' and Hgt.exists_arch prove HasIwasawa at each place for the Hermitian form xi J^T on the doubled space (xi = 1 if Y is Hermitian, xi = x - c(x) if skew-Hermitian, Hgt.exists_scal), whose unitary group is G_Y after transposition (Hgt.mem_HR, Hgt.back). At a finite place the Lean proves it from a basis of L_v whose Gram matrix is a unit times a local generator delta (gram_loc, using that L is its own dual for h, or for the trace form when Y is skew-Hermitian) and an integral t with t + c(t) = 1 from the good base, through hasIwasawa_of_frame' and lagr_orbit'; the stabilizer of L_v + L_v is then a special maximal compact subgroup, and the statement is the Iwasawa decomposition G = PK of Bruhat-Tits for it [BT72], [Car79, 3.5]. At an infinite place the subgroup is the maximal compact subgroup of elements unitary for the doubled Cartan involution (exists_arch through hasIwasawa_arch and exists_cartan_frame), and the statement is G = PK as in [MW95, I.1.4]. The Lean statements are these published decompositions for these subgroups.
asm-theta-agree-doubling-stabilizer: HgtEx (hgtEx_of stab2Cpt) gives K with IsStab2, a with IsHgt, continuity and positivity, and the continuous embedding emb2 with IsEmb; Stab2Cpt gives (1). The Lean does not state uniqueness, but IsStab2 is an iff and IsHgt.iwa determines a, which hgtInt_of and normZeta_of use to identify any two such K and a.
asm-theta-agree-doubling-count: count_ad is stated for a closed subgroup H of the units of an A-algebra B with continuous linear coordinates; the book takes B = M_n(A_E). Its Omega and Omega_0 are as here; |u| is absE. The proof uses rho from exists_rho, scale_ad and count_grp with exists_cover.
asm-theta-agree-doubling-integrable: HgtInt, by hgtInt_of stab2Cpt, for the K, a and e of HgtEx; T and T' are toRows_1 and toRows_2 of mat2 k^{-1} times diagCols.
asm-theta-agree-doubling-frame: FrameConj, by frameConj; the frame is IsFrame2 with the standard compact subgroup IsStdK, and the conclusion is k in K iff p^{-1} k p in K_0, with IsPar p t.
asm-theta-agree-doubling-continuation: EisContinues, by eisContinues_of EisBL FrameConj. Its conclusion is IsEisCont (isOpen, conn, disc, half, hol, cont, grow) and IsRegAt at every point, which are (1) to (5). The hypothesis chi|A^x = eta^c is ResEtaPow. In grow the neighbourhood is a ball around s.
asm-theta-agree-doubling-datum: (1) is DblW (dblW) and (2) is DblX (dblX), both from dbl_main; the form of e-box is IsDblCoord, respectively IsDblCoordX. The Lean writes chi(det h')^{-1} as detInv chi h', and l is lD, the extension of Phi -> integral of Phi(u, u) for adeleMeasurePi. (3) is lD_haar.
asm-theta-agree-doubling-level: (1) is FinLevel (finLevel); the set Lambda consists of u whose coordinates dd.e u have zero archimedean components, and K-stability is actB k u in Lambda, which is u k^T. (2) is Gs.gau and Gs.same for the predicate Gs e tau eps theta theta'; Gs.gau gives more, a Gau structure (nowhere zero, logarithmic derivative a symmetric form with negative definite real part), of which the statement keeps only that f vanishes nowhere; the proof of the second claim uses the whole structure, which is Lemma asm-theta-agree-doubling-level-gaussian(1). Gs takes any A-linear isomorphism e and any matrices theta and theta', with no symplectic or Cartan condition, as the book does.
asm-theta-agree-doubling-level-gaussian: (1) is Box.gau_of, whose conclusion is the structure Box.Gau (ne, der, symm, neg), through Twist.schwartz_logDeriv_linear_gaussian and schwartz_logDeriv_linear_formula (the formula f(y) = f(0) exp(m(y, y)/2)). (2) is Box.opp, stated with dop a L f = the derivative of f in the direction a plus (-2 pi i) L f. (3) is Twist.FockLogDeriv.main, where T is given by the hypothesis that T(y, b) = 0 for all y forces b = 0; the Lean uses it with T(y, b) = linForm b y, the trace form.
asm-theta-agree-doubling-section: (1) is BoxSec (boxSec_of FinLevel Stab2Cpt) and (2) is BoxSecX (boxSecX_of); the finiteness under K is membership in Box.kfin, from polData_kfin and box_kfin. The Lean also assumes that the model is good, which holds for the model of a Weil pair.
asm-theta-agree-doubling-siegel-weil: (1) is SWAniso and (2) is SWAnisoX, the two halves of siegelWeilAniso_of SiegelWeilStd FrameConj FinLevel Stab2Cpt; the conclusion is EisValueAt, and the average over the domain is the Lean's set average. In SWAniso the measure and domain are those of the model; in SWAnisoX they are any Haar measure and fundamental domain.
asm-theta-agree-doubling-value: SWFull (swFull_of SWAniso EisContinues BoxSec) and SWFullX (swFullX_of SWAnisoX EisContinues BoxSecX), through IsEisCont.update.
asm-theta-agree-doubling-kernel: kpair_cont, with the kernel pairing kpair chi e mu D (E-hat s) phi as P(s, phi), the law of f as Law chi z f, and Cpt (Lemma asm-theta-agree-definite-compact) for the compactness facts; t_1 is max t (t_0 + Re s_0 - Re z). The unfolding is unfold0 (the hypothesis Unfold0) and the coset description is orbit.
asm-theta-agree-nonvanishing-euler: (1) is Dbl.LocMeas (locMeas: Measure.haarMeasure on the positive compacts given by the integral elements, isCompact_int and isOpen_int). (2) is Dbl.EulerProd (eulerProd): Euler.step for one place, from the general Euler.factor (Fubini on H x G with the skew map (u, g) -> (u, u g), and pres_right for the right invariance on K), then induction over S and tendsto_setIntegral_of_monotone, with ae_mulVec for the union. The Lean states the limit as Tendsto along atTop on Finset {v // v not in T}.
asm-theta-agree-nonvanishing-normalizer: Dbl.DProd, proved by dProd: euler_half gives, for each factor i, d_i = exp(-sum log(1 + x_v)) with the summability of N(v)^(-s) for s > 1 (Cheb.summable_absNorm_rpow_ideal); hasProd_prod multiplies them.
asm-theta-agree-nonvanishing-unramified: Dbl.LocUnr, discharged by locUnr_of LocUnrSplit LocUnrInert (locUnrSplit and Inert.main), after KFinLoc.split_or_inert: under the conditions on the base every finite place is split or inert in E. Relation to the literature: the unramified computation of the doubling zeta integral for the trivial representation of U(X), Z_v(s) = L_v(s + 1/2, 1 x chi)/d_v(s), the Satake parameters of the trivial representation giving the product over i [GPSR87; Li92 for unitary groups]. The Lean states it for any function with the spherical law at v for the lattice stabilizer of the doubled space, whose value is only fixed on P K at v, and proves it its own way.
asm-theta-agree-nonvanishing-pair: Dbl.pair_ne_zero HgtEx NormZeta EulerProd LocMeas LocUnr BadFactor RealInv DProd (BotAsm.lean). The identity is key: tendsto_nhds_unique of EulerProd times DProd against hasProd_prod of the local L-factors, with hasProd_off for the factors at T; the continuation is eq_zero_of_right (U complement countable, U meet the right half-plane connected through psi(w) = exp(Re w) + i Im w, identity theorem); the conclusion uses the hypothesis on Lambda at the integers k - i, where d = 2k. The hypothesis on chi_X is used only in BadFactor.
asm-theta-agree-nonvanishing-hecke: Dbl.LInt2, proved by lInt2 (ConstOfGood.lean): exists_hchar_unitary gives a unitary Hecke character H with the local components of nu and infinity type m_alpha - m_beta (hasExp_nu), and ThKRed.HK.heckeL_ne_zero gives Lambda, the completed L-function times the conductor power and the inverse gamma factors, with the cases z >= 1 and z <= 0 through continuation_ne_zero_of_one_le_re for mu and mu^-1 and the root numbers; the bound |m(w)| > a + a' is the field kappa of Geo.IsGood. Relation to the literature: Hecke's continuation and functional equation and the nonvanishing on Re s >= 1 [Hec20; Tat67], which the Lean takes from its own Hecke L-function library.
asm-theta-agree-nonvanishing-bottom: Dbl.NonZeroBot, proved by nonZeroBottom_of_doubling_integral KReal LInt2 HgtEx NormZeta EulerProd LocMeas LocUnr BadFactor RealInv DProd, which applies pair_ne_zero to pairV with chi_W = nu^-1 (hr.quot, and LInt2 at nu^-1) and to pairV' with chi_W = nu (hr.quot', and LInt2 at nu); the nontriviality of Pi is hr.nontriv.
asm-theta-agree-definite: ThK.PolZero, proved by ThKR.polynomial_vanishing_of_compactness from SiegelWeilStd, EisBL and Published.HeckeLEntireAndNonzeroAtOne and the properties NonZeroAn, Factor, MatchEx, ThetaBasic, WeilConv, KDecay, ICont, GrpTop, EpsOf, SiegelAll, FinVolU and Unimod. Its body is Dbl.polZero_of with CptAll = cptAll_of (Lemma asm-theta-agree-definite-compact), HermLine = hermLine_of' (Lemma asm-theta-agree-definite-line), CoefLine = coefLine_of (Lemma asm-theta-agree-definite-norms) and ThConst = thConst_of' (Lemma asm-theta-agree-definite-constant). The proof follows polZero_of: c is the lam of HermLine for (1,0,0,1), orth gives Step 2, lam comes from HermLine for (1,-c,1,-c), key (with int_th) is Step 4, l0 is Step 5 and main is Step 6. PolSch (polSch) gives that polynomial data are Schwartz-Bruhat. Lemma asm-theta-agree-definite-inputs supplies the inputs.
asm-theta-agree-definite-volume: ThKEst.FinVolU (proved as finVolU, through fv_exists_herm and fundamental_domain_finite_volume) and ThKF.Unimod (proved as unimodularity_holds, through unimodLC), both for a nondegenerate epsilon-Hermitian matrix over a CM field. The finite volume is the theorem of Borel and Harish-Chandra [BHC62] for the restriction of scalars to Q of the unitary group of J, which has no nontrivial rational characters; unimodularity holds for every reductive group [Bor69]. Unimod also gives the countability of U_J(F) and a Haar measure with a fundamental domain. The Lean proves both in its own way; the statements are the published ones specialised to these groups.
asm-theta-agree-definite-products: pet mu D f f' is the Bochner integral of f * star f' over D, which is 0 when the integrand is not integrable; the book uses it only for integrable products. IsRapid phi asks phi continuous, invariant under ratU on the left, and norm(phi h) * qht(h)^N bounded for every N, where qht is the infimum of ht over the coset ratU * h. th om mu D phi Psi g = pet mu D phi (theta om Psi g). pairs B G X R Rf is the set of y with y.2 in G.M'.So and PolMatch y.1 y.2, and comb G om om' s t y = s * I(y.1) + t * I'(y.2).
asm-theta-agree-definite-compact: Cpt sigma Y.J has the fields lc, sc, t2, cnt (part 1), cov and hgt (part 2, with qht), ex, fin and right (part 3). CptAll asks Cpt for every Hermitian or skew-Hermitian lattice space with min r s = 0, and cptAll_of proves it from GrpTop, EpsOf, SiegelAll, FinVolU and Unimod: the Witt torus of SiegelAll has size 0 by EpsOf, so its map is constant 1. mu(D) > 0 is fd_ne, inside Cpt.vol_ne. Part 4 is Cpt.bdd, Cpt.bdd₂ and Cpt.eq_zero (through fd_eq_zero), and part 5 is Cpt.rapid.
asm-theta-agree-definite-continuous: The first clause of ThKF.ICont; its second clause, for elements of So when om preserves So, is not used here. ICont is a property used by ThKR.polynomial_vanishing_of_compactness and proved outside it, as ThKEst.iCont = iCont_of thetaBasic grpTop_of epsOf_of (domWeil_of_U domWeilU) domSoU soFin_of. iCont_of writes Phi as a sum of pure tensors (soFin_of, dom_sum) and applies dom_continuous, dominated convergence with the domination of Lemma asm-theta-agree-convergence-dominated.
asm-theta-agree-definite-inputs: Properties of the proof of PolZero; all ten proofs are written out, (2) from Lemmas asm-theta-agree-definite-inputs-growth-lattice and -growth-inputs. The proof of (2) follows theta_moderate_growth_of_decay with weil_rep_bounded_denominator. The proof of (10) follows coefLine_of up to its term val, for the Weil pair pairV' T and the lattice stabilizer of the doubled space of W. (1) Dbl.PolRank, proved by polRank. (2) The bound in the first clause of ThK.ThetaBasic. (3) TC.inv_loc together with the clauses of TC.SplitModel that TC.const_of uses: the first sentence is the lifting clause of SplitModel, and the hypothesis asks the invariance of L for one h in U_W at v above each h0 in GL_d(F_v), as inv_loc does; Lemma asm-theta-agree-definite-constant supplies it from the invariance for all h. (4) Dbl.ConstOfGood, proved by SA.constOfGood from Published.HeckeLEntireAndNonzeroAtOne_holds; the proof follows it: L is the subgroup of the x with f(x g) = f(g) for all g, conj_mem_UAt gives the conjugates, and SA.mem_of_good is eq_top_of_lines with HasLines from exists_line and normOne_mem. (8) Dbl.PairsStable and (9) Dbl.PairsIrr, proved by pairsStable and pairsIrr (PairsFin.lean); the proof of (9) follows pairsIrr_of = pairsIrr_of_arch A.archOp, with C_T1 the span Cl of the Lean, polMatch_iff and polMatch_big for the description of correspondence, and Prs.fill. (10) The conclusions of kpair_cont and of the term val of coefLine_of, for the continuation Ê of SWFull at the section x -> l(om2 x (boxFun Psi (star Psi))) of BoxSec: Z_phi(z) is kpair alpha e mu D (Ê z) phi, the integral over D x D of Ê(e(h,h')) alpha(det h')^{-1} phi(h') conj(phi(h)), and F_z(g) = flat a f z0 z (e(1,g)) alpha(det g)^{-1} for the embedding e of U_W x U_W into the doubled group and the height function a of a lattice stabilizer (HgtEx, HgtInt, Stab2Cpt). The factor 2 is the constant of Theorem asm-theta-agree-siegel-weil for n = a + a' >= m = a'. SWFull comes from SiegelWeilStd and EisBL through siegelWeilAniso_of and eisContinues_of, which Lemma asm-theta-agree-nonvanishing also uses. The proof of (1) follows polRank: G_eps is the infimum over p of the kernels of dL (J p) - I dL p (exists_vac), J comes from Dense.exists_real_structure with the signs eps, the positivity uses trace_symp, e and hf_neg, the injectivity of f -> f 0 is ode_zero, and N is exists_stable for the dL of a real basis, with actsD_unique for the first-order actions. The proof of (3) follows inv_loc: the reduction to pure tensors is eqOn_span' and schA_le, Psi[psi] is intersection_update_fsHerm_neg_one, Q is beta, and the equivariance of Q under GL_n(F_v) is locBil (Lemma asm-theta-agree-definite-dist-bilinear). The proof of (7) follows goodNe: the embedding is nonempty_emb_of_splitsFully (KFinLoc.split_or_inert, which uses that E/F is unramified, SplitFullyNorm.exists_prime_absNorm_eq_of_splitsFully and Ideal.absNorm_algebraMap), and the value is nu_pow_ne_one for k = 1, through ChrWUnif.chrW_unifAt, HeckeBridge.exists_hchar, hasExp_nu, the field kappa of Geo.IsGood and Lemma asm-theta-agree-definite-hecke. Lemma asm-theta-agree-coinvariants-split proves the embedding in another way (KCo.good_split_of_cm). The proof of (8) follows pairsStable_of: the first claim is pairs_lin (polMatch_add_smul), and the second is ThKEnd.MatchStab (Lemma asm-theta-agree-end-stable) for k = h, which lies in FinK (the set K^theta_W) by comm_theta, as cartan_one makes theta_{W,w} = 1 for a definite W.

asm-theta-agree-end-two-step-kill: Part (1) is Two.emb2, defined as Dual.emb of dual2 (the map embM), with emb2_mulVec_incV_x_and_complement_x, emb2_dia_mulVec_incV_y, emb2_mulVec_complement_eq and emb2_dia_isLevi; the formula in the statement is embM. asm-theta-agree-end-kill-siegel-reductio: Formalism.D.siegelSetsSL2Adelic, for any number field, supplied to siegel_ad by Classical.siegelSetsSL2Adelic_tie, which is GroundTheory.BlockD.siegelSetsSL2Adelic_holds: Alpöge proves it from the Lean's Siegel sets for GL_2 over the adeles (exists_siegelSet).
